title: Client sessions and protocol
scope:
This category covers everything a CephFS client sees of an MDS below the level of individual operations: the transport (msgr1, msgr2.1 crc and secure modes, compression negotiation, connection policy, replay of unacknowledged messages, peer-reset signalling, entity names and addresses), cephx on the service side (the parsing of MDS caps into the session is catalogued with the auth caps in 11), the encoding conventions, the client message catalog and the field-level encoding of every client message (requests, replies, traces, InodeStat, DirStat, LeaseStat, snap traces, extra_bl payloads, caps, cap releases, leases, snaps, quota, metrics, quarantine), the CephFS and connection feature bits with the first kernel and Ceph release of each bit and each protocol fallback, client metadata, the session life cycle (open, admission, renew, stale, autoclose, close, kill, eviction with blocklisting), the reconnect protocol after an MDS failover, the NFS-Ganesha reclaim protocol, request forwarding and retries, and the client-specific expectations of the Linux kernel client, libcephfs, ceph-fuse, NFS-Ganesha and Samba. It also records the obligations the embedded MonClient, MgrClient and Objecter place on an MDS process, because they share the MDS messenger and identity.

Sources are the fact-checked map pages wire-protocol, sessions, kclient-expectations, libcephfs-fuse-ganesha-expectations and transport-auth-and-client-library-contract, plus the staging notes of the items wire-protocol, sessions, kclient and libcephfs. Entries taken only from the transport page have empty staging_refs.

Excluded, and catalogued elsewhere: the semantics of capabilities, cap recall, dentry leases, async dirops and delegated inode numbers (03-caps-leases-and-locking); every request op handler, the completed-request table, request batching, file locks, xattrs, vxattrs, ACLs, fscrypt and inline-data semantics (04-namespace-and-posix-operations); snap realms, quotas and subvolume ids (08-snapshots-quotas-subvolumes); SessionMap persistence, ESession events and inode preallocation tables (06-journal-and-storage); metrics, the dmClock queue and quarantine (10-qos-metrics-quiesce-quarantine); MDS auth cap grammar, session admin commands, health warnings and perf counters (11-security-admin-and-observability); MDSMap, rank states and the recovery state machine (01-cluster-membership-and-ha). Where an entry here touches one of those mechanisms it describes only the wire or session part and links to the owning map page.

Cross-category review (2026-10-11): entries that duplicated an entry of the owning category were retired (listed under "retired" in features.json with the entry they were merged into) or shortened to pointers whose description starts with "See F-XXX-NNN." and keeps only the facts specific to this category.

features.group: Transport: msgr2 (and legacy msgr1) as clients see them
features.name: msgr1 (legacy protocol) server side for client connections
features.summary: Accepting side of the legacy messenger protocol, used only by a Linux kernel mounted without ms_mode (old mon:/path device syntax, mon_addr= without ms_mode, or ms_mode=legacy) and by Ceph clients 13.x and older.
features.description: The server writes the banner "ceph v027", its legacy 136-byte address and the client socket address, then reads the client banner, the 33-byte ceph_msg_connect and the authorizer. A protocol_version other than 32 (CEPH_MDSC_PROTOCOL) from a client peer gets the reply tag BADPROTOVER; other reply tags are READY, SEQ, RETRY_SESSION, RETRY_GLOBAL, RESETSESSION, WAIT, BADAUTHORIZER, FEATURES and CHALLENGE_AUTHORIZER, and replacing an existing connection costs one extra RETRY_GLOBAL round trip. In the open state every MSG carries a 53-byte header (crc32c over the first 49 bytes), front/middle/data crcs and, when MSG_AUTH was negotiated, a 21-byte footer with a cephx signature (13-byte old footer otherwise); ACK carries le64 in_seq and KEEPALIVE2 is answered with KEEPALIVE2_ACK. The kernel requires MSG_AUTH in the READY/SEQ reply features (unless mounted with nocephx_sign_messages), accepts only MSG, ACK, KEEPALIVE2_ACK and CLOSE in the open state, rejects WAIT, accepts only in_seq + 1 as the next sequence number, and limits front and middle to 16 MiB and data to 64 MiB.
gates: kernel mount without ms_mode or with ms_mode=legacy (the kernel's built-in default; mount.ceph passes ms_mode=prefer-crc for the new device syntax unless ms_mode or mon_addr is given)
features.notes: Client generations: a kernel uses msgr1 only when mounted without ms_mode; mount.ceph has passed ms_mode=prefer-crc for the new device syntax since commit 9663f8aaec9 (first released in 17.2.0); kernels before v5.11 have no msgr2 code at all; Ceph clients 13.x and older speak only msgr1, 14.x and later connect to the first (v2) address of the vector (kclient expectations 7.1.2, msgr row). No CephFS feature bit reveals msgr2 capability. Disabling ms_bind_msgr1 removes the v1 addresses from the MDSMap and a kernel without an ms_mode option then fails the MDSMap decode and shuts the mount down. The C++ messenger never sends the CLOSE tag; the kernel would move the connection to CLOSED for good on it. Only msgr1 negotiates the protocol number; msgr2 has no protocol-number check.

legacy.note: The C++ MDS speaks msgr1 only to peers that dial its v1 address: a kernel mounted without ms_mode (old mon:/path device syntax, mon_addr= without ms_mode, or ms_mode=legacy) and Ceph clients 13.x and older. mount.ceph passes ms_mode=prefer-crc for the new device syntax since commit 9663f8aaec9 (first released in 17.2.0), and libcephfs, ceph-fuse and NFS-Ganesha dial the first entry of the address vector, which is the v2 one. Rook v1.21.0 gives ceph-csi kernel mounts ms_mode=prefer-crc and the v2 monitor port only when requireMsgr2 or compression is set (ms_mode=secure with encryption; its example cluster.yaml sets requireMsgr2: true), and passes no ms_mode with monitor port 6789 under the CRD default requireMsgr2=false.

features.group: Transport: msgr2 (and legacy msgr1) as clients see them
features.name: msgr2.1 crc mode for client connections
features.summary: Frame-based messenger protocol revision 2.1 with crc32c integrity, used by C++ clients by default and by kernels mounted with ms_mode=crc or prefer-crc (mount.ceph passes prefer-crc for the new device syntax).
features.description: Banner "ceph v2\n" + le16 16 + le64 supported + le64 required; C++ advertises REVISION_1|COMPRESSION and requires nothing, the kernel advertises and requires REVISION_1 only. Every frame starts with a 32-byte preamble (tag, segment count 1-4, four length/alignment pairs, flags, crc32c over 28 bytes); in 2.1-crc segment 1 is followed by its crc and a 13-byte epilogue with crcs for segments 2-4 is present only in multi-segment frames, with crc32c(-1, empty) = 0xFFFFFFFF for an empty segment followed by a non-empty one and 0 for absent segments. Control frames are HELLO, AUTH_REQUEST, AUTH_BAD_METHOD, AUTH_REPLY_MORE, AUTH_REQUEST_MORE, AUTH_DONE, AUTH_SIGNATURE, CLIENT_IDENT, SERVER_IDENT, IDENT_MISSING_FEATURES, SESSION_RECONNECT/RESET/RETRY/RETRY_GLOBAL/RECONNECT_OK, WAIT, KEEPALIVE2(_ACK), ACK; MESSAGE carries the 41-byte ceph_msg_header2 (seq, tid, type, priority, version, ack_seq, compat_version). The kernel always verifies crcs (it ignores nocrc on msgr2), rejects empty or aborted control frames, WAIT, KEEPALIVE2 from the server and SESSION_RESET with full=0, and requires the first MSGR2 address of SERVER_IDENT to equal the dialled MDSMap address byte for byte and MSG_AUTH in the server supported features.
gates: kernel mount option ms_mode=crc|prefer-crc (kernels v5.11+; mount.ceph passes prefer-crc for the new device syntax)
features.notes: msgr2.0 framing (17-byte epilogue) is used only with a peer lacking REVISION_1; kernels and C++ clients are 2.1. C++ clients offer ms_client_mode "crc secure" and the server picks the first mode in the client list it allows, so C++ clients end up in crc mode. An MDS with ms_crc_data=false writes zero segment crcs and cannot serve msgr2-crc kernel mounts (transport page 8, item 11). msgr2 has no protocol-number check.

legacy_parts.note: msgr2.0 (rev0) frame layout (17-byte epilogue), selected per connection for peers whose banner lacks REVISION_1. The 7.3 kernel advertises and requires REVISION_1, and C++ peers at this commit advertise it, so every baseline connection uses msgr2.1 framing. The C++ server requires no msgr2 feature and switches a connection to msgr2.0 (rev0) framing when the peer's banner lacks REVISION_1. REVISION_1 first appears in Ceph 14.2.11, 15.2.5 and 16.1.0, so rev0 peers are Ceph 14.2.0-14.2.10 and 15.2.0-15.2.4 clients.

features.group: Transport: msgr2 (and legacy msgr1) as clients see them
features.name: msgr2.1 secure mode (AES-128-GCM)
features.summary: Encrypted msgr2.1 frames for clients that select secure mode (kernel ms_mode=secure or prefer-secure, or a C++ client configured for it).
features.description: After AUTH_DONE both sides derive AES-128-GCM handlers from the 64-byte connection secret carried in the CephXAuthorizeReply v2: bytes 0-15 are the key, 16-27 nonce A and 28-39 nonce B; the client receives with A and sends with B and the server does the opposite. A nonce is {le32 fixed, le64 counter} and msgr2.1 increments the 64-bit counter per encrypted unit. In 2.1-secure the first block is the preamble plus a 48-byte inline buffer with the start of segment 1 plus a 16-byte tag (96 bytes); the rest of segment 1 and segments 2-4 with a 16-byte epilogue follow as further encrypted units. Secure mode needs a cephx session key: with auth none only crc is offered and a client insisting on secure gets AUTH_BAD_METHOD. The kernel requires at least 40 and accepts at most 64 secret bytes.
features.notes: msgr2.0 secure mode increments a 32-bit nonce field and faults the connection with "out of nonces" when it would wrap (transport page 8, item 13); msgr2.1 does not have that limit. Secure mode is selected only on explicit client configuration; no default client path uses it towards an MDS.

legacy_parts.note: msgr2.0 secure-mode nonce format and frame layout (new_nonce_format=false) for peers without REVISION_1. Every baseline peer negotiates msgr2.1, whose secure mode increments a 64-bit nonce counter. The msgr2.0 nonce format (counter in the 32-bit field, connection fault 'out of nonces' on wrap) is chosen only for peers without REVISION_1, which are Ceph 14.2.0-14.2.10 and 15.2.0-15.2.4.

features.group: Transport: msgr2 (and legacy msgr1) as clients see them
features.name: msgr2 on-wire compression negotiation
features.summary: Optional COMPRESSION_REQUEST/COMPRESSION_DONE phase of msgr2; for MDS client connections it always negotiates no compression.
features.description: C++ messengers advertise the COMPRESSION banner bit; the phase runs only if both banners carry it, so it never runs with the kernel. The server answers COMPRESSION_REQUEST with COMPRESSION_DONE whose mode comes from CompressorRegistry::get_mode, which returns COMP_NONE for every peer type except OSD (ms_osd_compress_mode, default none) and for secure mode unless ms_compress_secure is set. A compressed frame sets FRAME_EARLY_DATA_COMPRESSED in the preamble flags; such a frame on a connection without negotiated compression trips ceph_assert_always in the C++ receiver.
features.notes: C++ clients run the handshake only when the server advertises the COMPRESSION bit; a server that does not advertise it skips the phase with them (transport page 7.4).

features.group: Transport: msgr2 (and legacy msgr1) as clients see them
features.name: Address vector publication and server identity checks
features.summary: The MDS listens on a v2 and, by default, a v1 address per IP, publishes them through its beacon into the MDSMap, and every client checks the server identity against that map entry.
features.description: With ms_bind_msgr1 and ms_bind_msgr2 (both default true) the address vector is [v2:ip:port/nonce, v1:ip:port/nonce] per IP, ports from ms_bind_port_min..max (6800-7568) and a random per-process nonce; clients learn it only from the MDSMap, never from the MDS. The kernel picks the first address of the type its ms_mode selects and fails the whole MDSMap decode (mount shut down) if an entry has addresses but none of that type. C++ clients connect to the first address they speak (the v2 one), require the SERVER_IDENT address vector to contain the dialled address, and match it for equality against the MDSMap address vector when handling a remote reset; the kernel requires the first MSGR2 address of SERVER_IDENT (or the msgr1 banner address, nonce included) to equal the dialled one. A restarted MDS has a new nonce, so clients see a new address in the MDSMap and open new connections. Only kernels mounted without ms_mode dial the v1 entry; with ms_bind_msgr1=false the vector holds only v2 entries.
features.notes: The same address vector is what the monitor uses to find the MDS for its mdsmap subscription and what OSD blocklisting fences (F-PROTO-106).

legacy_parts.note: Publication of a v1 (TYPE_LEGACY) address per IP (ms_bind_msgr1, default true) and the msgr1 banner address identity check. A 7.3 kernel mounted with ms_mode=prefer-crc takes only the first TYPE_MSGR2 address of each MDSMap entry and compares the first v2 address of SERVER_IDENT with the dialled one. C++ clients dial the first entry of the vector, which is the v2 address. The v1 entries and the kernel's msgr1 banner address check are used only by msgr1 peers: kernels mounted without ms_mode and Ceph clients 13.x and older.

features.group: Transport: msgr2 (and legacy msgr1) as clients see them
features.name: Lossless stateful-server connection policy and replay of unacknowledged messages
features.summary: Client connections never lose an acknowledged-pending message across a TCP fault: the MDS keeps sent messages until acked and replays them with their original sequence numbers when the client reconnects.
features.description: ceph-mds installs Policy::stateful_server(0) for client peers: lossless, server (the MDS never initiates TCP to a client), standby, resetcheck, no required connection features. Each direction numbers messages at write time (++out_seq); non-lossy connections keep written messages until acknowledged (msgr1 TAG_ACK with le64 in_seq; msgr2 ack_seq piggybacked on every MESSAGE or an ACK frame). On a transport fault the server-side connection goes to STANDBY and raises no event to the MDS; when the client reconnects (msgr1 SEQ exchange, msgr2 SESSION_RECONNECT with msg_seq answered by SESSION_RECONNECT_OK(in_seq)) the unacknowledged messages are requeued at priority 255 and resent with their original sequence numbers. Output is FIFO only among equal priorities on one connection; all MClient* messages use the default priority 127 except MClientMetrics.
features.notes: The kernel accepts no sequence gaps ("bad message sequence # for incoming message"); C++ receivers log gaps but drop a message with an old sequence number and, reading the code, then stop reading the connection (derived from code, unverified at runtime; transport page 8, item 3). Connection events are queued at priority 255 and can overtake messages still queued from the same connection (transport page 8, item 7). Session liveness is handled by the session layer, not by the messenger. See also F-CLU-109.

legacy_parts.note: msgr1 acknowledgement (TAG_ACK with le64 in_seq) and the msgr1 SEQ exchange on reconnect. On baseline (msgr2) client connections acknowledgements travel as ack_seq in MESSAGE or ACK frames, and reconnects use SESSION_RECONNECT answered by SESSION_RECONNECT_OK. The msgr1 TAG_ACK and the msgr1 SEQ exchange are reached only by kernels mounted without ms_mode and Ceph clients 13.x and older.

features.group: Transport: msgr2 (and legacy msgr1) as clients see them
features.name: Peer-reset detection and session-reset signalling
features.summary: How a client learns that the MDS side of its connection (or session) is gone, and how the MDS reacts when a client restarts its side.
features.description: With resetcheck, a peer that reconnects after dropping its own side is detected (msgr1 connect_seq 0 against an existing value above 0; msgr2 client-cookie mismatch); the MDS messenger then discards both queues of that peer and raises ms_handle_remote_reset. When the MDS side has no record of the session it answers the reconnect with RESETSESSION (msgr1) or SESSION_RESET(full=1) (msgr2). MDSDaemon reacts to resets only for closed sessions (mark_down, clear Connection::priv); open sessions survive connection loss. Before sending CEPH_SESSION_CLOSE the MDS marks the connection disposable so a client that missed CLOSE gets a reset on reconnect; killed (evicted) sessions get mark_down without CLOSE. The kernel (mds_peer_reset) sends MClientReconnect if the rank is in up:reconnect, ignores the reset if the rank is below it or the mount is fenced, and otherwise tears the session down locally; libcephfs treats a closing session as closed, reopens an opening one, and marks an open one stale (or closed with client_reconnect_stale) after requesting a fresh OSDMap to detect blocklisting.
features.notes: The kernel rejects SESSION_RESET(full=0) as a protocol error; the C++ server sends full=0 only for MDS peers and for its own half-established outgoing connections (transport page 8, item 15). A kernel whose session is torn down locally while the rank is active loses all caps of that session silently (kclient expectations 8).

legacy_parts.note: msgr1 remote-reset detection by connect_seq and the RESETSESSION reply. On msgr2 a client that restarted its side is detected by a client-cookie mismatch, and a lost server-side session is answered with SESSION_RESET(full=1). The msgr1 detection (connect_seq 0 against an existing value above 0) and the RESETSESSION reply tag are reached only by msgr1 peers.

features.group: Transport: msgr2 (and legacy msgr1) as clients see them
features.name: MDS entity name and rank identity on the wire
features.summary: Clients identify which rank a message came from by the MDS messenger name (mds.<rank>) or by the connection.
features.description: The MDS messenger is named mds.-1 (MDS_RANK_NONE) before a role is held, mds.<rank> once a rank is held and mds.<gid> in standby-replay. msgr1 copies the name into every message header; msgr2 sends the name number once as the SERVER_IDENT gid and the receiver stamps every message of the connection with it. libcephfs reads the sending rank as m->get_source().num() in its session, forward, snap, cap and reply handlers and drops messages whose (rank, connection) pair matches no session; the kernel keys MDS messages by the connection and checks only the peer entity type (CEPH_ENTITY_TYPE_MDS, 0x02) in HELLO. The MDS accepts session, reconnect, reclaim, caps, cap-release and lease messages only from CEPH_ENTITY_TYPE_CLIENT (0x08) peers.
features.notes: Because msgr2 fixes the name number at handshake, a connection established while the messenger had another number keeps that number for its lifetime; the C++ MDS renames its messenger before it becomes reachable as a rank (transport page 8, item 32). The kernel overwrites peer_name.num with the number the server reports (wire-protocol 8). The messenger starts with a random nonce per process and is renamed on every state change. The kernel also checks that the server address and nonce reported in SERVER_IDENT equal the map entry (linux/net/ceph/messenger_v2.c:2512 (process_server_ident)). See also F-CLU-109 (messenger policies), F-PROTO-106 (fencing identity).

legacy_parts.note: msgr1 per-message header src (entity name copied into each ceph_msg_header on the wire). On msgr2 the name number is sent once as the IDENT gid and the receiver stamps it on every message of the connection. Carrying the entity name in every message header on the wire is msgr1 framing and is reached only by msgr1 peers.

features.group: Transport: msgr2 (and legacy msgr1) as clients see them
features.name: Keepalives and connection timeouts
features.summary: Transport-level liveness between clients and the MDS: client keepalives, the server echo, and the messenger handshake and idle timeouts.
features.description: KEEPALIVE2 (msgr1 tag 14, msgr2 frame 18) carries a timestamp and is answered with KEEPALIVE2_ACK echoing it; the MDS itself never sends keepalives, and the kernel treats KEEPALIVE/KEEPALIVE2 from a server as a protocol error. The kernel sends a keepalive or a REQUEST_RENEWCAPS to each MDS session every time its housekeeping work runs (at most 5 s apart). The C++ messenger faults a handshake that makes no progress within ms_connection_ready_timeout (10 s) and an established connection idle for ms_connection_idle_timeout (900 s).

legacy_parts.note: msgr1 KEEPALIVE2 tag handling. Baseline peers exchange KEEPALIVE2 and KEEPALIVE2_ACK as msgr2 frames. The msgr1 tag form (tag 14 and its ack) is reached only by msgr1 peers.

features.group: Transport: msgr2 (and legacy msgr1) as clients see them
features.name: Inbound flow control (messenger dispatch throttle)
features.summary: The only inbound back-pressure of the C++ MDS messenger: one byte budget shared by all connections.
features.description: ceph_mds.cc installs no per-policy message or byte throttlers, so both protocols skip their per-connection throttles. Each message size (front + middle + data) is taken from the messenger-wide ms_dispatch_throttle_bytes budget (100 MiB) after the msgr1 header or msgr2 preamble is read; when it is exhausted the connection stops reading its socket and retries every ms_client_throttle_retry_time_interval (5000 us), so a slow dispatcher pushes back on every peer through TCP. The budget is returned after dispatch or when queued messages are discarded. Nothing bounds a connection output queue.
features.notes: Reading the code, a dropped old-sequence message never returns its dispatch-throttle bytes (derived from code, unverified; transport page 3.3).

legacy_parts.note: ProtocolV1::throttle_dispatch_queue (throttle taken after the msgr1 header). For baseline peers the messenger-wide dispatch throttle is taken after the msgr2 preamble is read. The msgr1 throttle point (after the msgr1 message header) is reached only by msgr1 peers.

features.name: cephx authorizer verification for service mds
features.summary: Every client connection authenticates with a cephx authorizer for service type mds, verified by the MDS (through its MonClient auth-server hooks) against rotating service secrets.
features.description: The authorizer is {u8 1, le64 global_id, le32 service_id = 2 (MDS), CephXTicketBlob {u8 1, le64 secret_id, ticket encrypted with a rotating secret}, CephXAuthorize encrypted with the ticket session key {magic, nonce, have_challenge, server_challenge + 1}}. Verification selects the keyring key for secret_id -1 or one of the held rotating secrets, decrypts the ticket, checks the global id, the default auid, allow_all false and a caps blob of exactly one string. A CEPHX_V2 peer first gets a challenge (msgr1 CHALLENGE_AUTHORIZER, msgr2 AUTH_REPLY_MORE with the raw ciphertext) and resends the authorizer with challenge + 1; the reply is CephXAuthorizeReply {nonce + 1, connection secret (64 random bytes in secure mode, empty in crc mode or msgr1)}. The service does not compare ticket expiry with its clock: a ticket is accepted while its secret_id is one of the at most three held secrets. Both key types occur: CEPH_CRYPTO_AES (1) and CEPH_CRYPTO_AES256KRB5 (2), depending on the cluster history; the kernel implements both. An empty authorizer fails (the MDS messenger requires one).
gates: cephx_service_require_version (default 2, adds CEPHX_V2 to msgr1 requirements)
features.notes: msgr1 BADAUTHORIZER makes the kernel retry once with a fresh authorizer and fail at the second. Ticket expiry is not checked by the service (transport page 8, item 18). When the MonMap auth_epoch grows the MonClient wipes rotating secrets and client authorizers fail until new ones arrive (item 19). See also F-ADM-002 (caps loading at accept), F-PROTO-012 (rotating secrets).

legacy_parts.note: msgr1 authorizer exchange: CHALLENGE_AUTHORIZER/BADAUTHORIZER reply tags, the msgr1 CEPHX_V2 requirement and no-challenge path, the empty msgr1 connection secret, and the kernel BADAUTHORIZER retry. Over msgr2 the authorizer challenge travels in AUTH_REPLY_MORE and the reply carries a 64-byte connection secret in secure mode or none in crc mode. The msgr1 exchange (CHALLENGE_AUTHORIZER and BADAUTHORIZER tags, CEPHX_V2 added to the msgr1 required features by cephx_service_require_version, no challenge for peers without CEPHX_V2, the kernel's single BADAUTHORIZER retry) is reached only by kernels mounted without ms_mode and Ceph clients 13.x and older.

features.name: Rotating mds service secrets
features.summary: The MDS keeps the current set of rotating mds service secrets from the monitors; without them no client authorizer can be verified.
features.description: Daemons of type MDS need rotating keys. The MonClient requests them with MAuth CEPHX_GET_ROTATING_KEY when fewer than three are held or the current one expired before now - min(30 s, auth_service_ticket_ttl/4), at most once per second; the monitor returns the whole RotatingSecrets map (previous, current, next) encrypted with the MDS key. The monitor seals service tickets with the current secret and ticket lifetimes are auth_service_ticket_ttl (1 h). At boot the MDS waits for rotating secrets (rotating_keys_bootstrap_timeout 30 s, max_rotating_auth_attempts 10). A MonMap whose auth_epoch increased wipes all rotating secrets and tickets.
features.notes: Boot-time waiting is described in auth-and-mds-caps 3.2 (owned by 11-security-admin-and-observability). See also F-ADM-001 (MDS self-authentication and keyring).

features.name: msgr1 message signatures
features.summary: Per-message cephx signatures on msgr1 connections, which a kernel mounted without ms_mode verifies by default.
features.description: With cephx_sign_messages (default true) msgr1 signs every message and checks signatures when MSG_AUTH was negotiated; the 64-bit signature goes into the 21-byte footer. Without CEPHX_V2 on the peer it is the first 8 bytes of AES-encrypt({1, magic, 16, header_crc, front_crc, middle_crc, data_crc}); with CEPHX_V2 it is the XOR of the four le64 words of AES-encrypt (AES keys) or HMAC-SHA256 (AES256KRB5 keys) over {header_crc, front_crc, front_len, middle_crc, middle_len, data_crc, data_len, low 32 bits of seq}. On msgr1 connections (a kernel mounted without ms_mode) the kernel signs and verifies every message unless mounted with nocephx_sign_messages; over msgr2, which mount.ceph selects for the new device syntax, it signs nothing (signing exists only in linux/net/ceph/messenger_v1.c). msgr2 has no per-message signature: AUTH_SIGNATURE (HMAC-SHA256 with the session key over all bytes received during the pre-auth phase) binds the handshake, and secure mode authenticates frames by GCM.

legacy.note: Per-message signing and checking exist only in the msgr1 implementations (C++ ProtocolV1, kernel messenger_v1), so only kernels mounted without ms_mode and Ceph clients 13.x and older use them. A search for sign_message and check_message_signature finds no call in src/msg/async/ProtocolV2.cc or linux/net/ceph/messenger_v2.c. Over msgr2 the AUTH_SIGNATURE frame (F-PROTO-002) binds the handshake and secure mode authenticates frames with AES-GCM.

features.name: Connection-to-session binding (identity is the cephx global id)
features.summary: Each client entity (client.<global_id>) has one session per rank; a connection is bound to it when it is accepted, and messages to a session without a connection are queued.
features.description: ms_handle_accept (under mds_lock) looks up the session by entity_name_t(peer_type, peer_global_id); if none exists it creates a bootstrap Session in state closed that is not inserted in the SessionMap, stores it in Connection::priv, copies auth_name, socket address and name into the session, and flushes the session preopen_out_queue. Every later message finds its session through Connection::priv; for CEPH_MSG_CLIENT_SESSION MDSRank::get_session can re-point the connection to an imported session of the same entity. Sends to a session without a connection are appended to preopen_out_queue. A remount gets a new global id and therefore a new session.
features.notes: MDSRank::get_session flushes only the bootstrap session queue when it re-points a connection to an imported session; messages queued on the imported session are sent only by ms_handle_accept (code observation, race not tested; sessions 8).

features.name: Encoding primitives and versioned-struct rules
features.summary: Little-endian Ceph encoding with ENCODE_START framing; client-facing versioned records always use struct_compat 1 and only append fields.
features.description: Integers are little-endian; bool is one byte; string, bufferlist and vector<u8> are u32 length + bytes; containers are u32 count + elements; utime_t/ceph_timespec are u32 sec + u32 nsec; filepath is u8 1, u64 ino, string (ino 0 = relative); frag_t u32; fragtree map<frag_t, i32>; interval_set u32 count + (start, len) pairs; errors travel as errorcode32_t (Linux errno). ENCODE_START(v, compat) writes u8 struct_v, u8 struct_compat, u32 length; DECODE_START throws if compat exceeds what the decoder knows and DECODE_FINISH skips unread trailing bytes. Client-facing sub-encodings use struct_compat 1 (InodeStat 9/1, DirStat 1/1, LeaseStat 2/1, quota_info_t 1/1, openc_response_t 1/1, getvxattr 1/1, SnapRealmInfoNew 2/1, optmetadata 1/1, MDSCapAuth/MDSCapMatch 1/1, BlockDiff 1/1). Raw packed structs (ceph_mds_request_head_legacy, reply head, caps head, cap items, session head) are memcpy-encoded.
features.notes: The kernel requires struct_compat == 1 on InodeStat, DirStat, LeaseStat and quota_info_t and uses struct_len to skip unknown trailing fields, but parses MDSCapAuth/MDSCapMatch positionally without struct_len (F-ADM-021). The stated interoperability rule is n-2 releases between daemons and n-3 for clients (doc/dev/encoding.rst, transport page 3.10).

features.name: Client message catalog and peer-type filtering
features.summary: The set of client message types, their versions, segments and directions, and which peer types the MDS accepts each from.
features.description: Types: 22 MClientSession (both, v7/compat 1), 23 MClientReconnect (C to M, v5/compat 4, payload in the data segment), 24 MClientRequest (C to M, v6/compat 1, front + data), 25 MClientRequestForward (M to C, v1), 26 MClientReply (M to C, v1), 27 MClientReclaim and 28 MClientReclaimReply (v1), 29 MClientMetrics (C to M), 0x310 MClientCaps (both, v14, xattrs in the middle segment), 0x311 MClientLease (both), 0x312 MClientSnap, 0x313 MClientCapRelease (v2), 0x314 MClientQuota, 0x315 MQuarantineDisable. header.tid carries the request tid (requests, replies, forwards) and the cap-flush tid (MClientCaps). Session, reconnect, reclaim, caps, cap-release and lease messages are accepted only from client peers and metrics only from client peers; MClientRequest and MClientReply are not filtered because ranks also exchange them (stray reintegration, quota realm creation). The MDS sends MMDSMap only to MDS peers; the kernel nevertheless accepts MDS_MAP and FS_MAP_USER on an MDS connection.
features.notes: Because CEPH_MSG_CLIENT_REPLY is not filtered by peer type, an unsafe MClientReply sent by a client reaches ceph_assert(reply->is_safe()) in Server::handle_client_reply and aborts the MDS (wire-protocol 8). MDS-originated MClientRequest/MClientReply between ranks are an internal use of the client message types.

features.name: Decode failures and client-triggerable aborts
features.summary: What the C++ MDS does with malformed or unexpected client input; unmodified clients do not send any of it.
features.description: Userspace peers decode in the messenger worker: an unknown type, a compat_version above the local HEAD_VERSION or a buffer::error makes decode_message return null and the connection faults (the kernel instead logs and drops unknown types). A ceph_assert inside decode_payload aborts the process: MClientCaps whose middle length differs from xattr_len, and MClientReply, MClientSnap or MClientQuota with trailing front bytes (the MDS decodes every known type before checking whether it accepts it). Under mds_lock: an MClientLease action other than RELEASE/RENEW/REVOKE_ACK on a held lease reaches ceph_abort(); handler-side decodes without try (initial-xattr map of new-inode ops, fscrypt last-block header of a truncating SETATTR, reconnect flock blob) throw out of the dispatcher; an owner uid/gid of -1 on a new-inode op trips ceph_assert in Server::prepare_new_inode. MKSNAP and SNAP_METADATA payloads are decoded inside try.
features.notes: All of these are derived from code (wire-protocol 8). Sending a message type a C++ peer does not know breaks that connection (transport page 3.10).

features.name: Golden encodings and encoding test data
features.summary: Tooling and reference data that pin the wire encodings: ceph-dencoder registrations, ceph-object-corpus, frame layout tables and crypto vectors.
features.description: ceph-dencoder registers the MClient* and MMDS* messages, cephx structures (CephXAuthorize, CephXTicketBlob, RotatingSecrets, CryptoKey, ...), entity addresses and OSDMap/MonMap/MgrMap types and supports import/decode/dump_json, encode, select_test and is_deterministic. ceph-object-corpus (git submodule, not initialised in this workspace) holds archived encodings per release, checked by readable.sh and check-generated.sh. msgr2 frame layouts in all four modes are tabulated in src/test/msgr/test_frames_v2.cc, AES256KRB5 vectors from RFC 8009 in src/test/crypto.cc. Not registered: MOSDBackoff, the msgr1 raw structs and every msgr2 frame.
features.notes: Message::encode has a dump block guarded by ENCODE_DUMP, which nothing in the tree defines (transport page 3.10).

features.name: CephFS feature bitmap exchange at session open
features.summary: Client and MDS exchange variable-length CephFS feature bitmaps in MClientSession; every feature-gated MDS decision tests the client bitmap, and clients pick decoders from the MDS bitmap.
features.description: feature_bitset_t is u32 byte length + little-endian u64 words (bit n in word n/64); a trailing partial word is tolerated on decode. The client sends its bits in REQUEST_OPEN (message v3+); the MDS stores them in session client_metadata.features and tests them with session->info.has_feature(bit). The MDS advertises CEPHFS_FEATURES_MDS_SUPPORTED = bits 0..24 (word 0x0000000001ffffff) and metric_spec bits 0..16 (0x1ffff) in OPEN, but only to clients that advertised MIMIC (bit 8); without it OPEN is sent as v1. Both clients overwrite their copy of the MDS bits on every OPEN: the kernel keeps only the first 64 bits (s_features) and needs a non-zero length of at least 8 bytes, libcephfs keeps the full bitset and the metric flags. The kernel 7.3 advertises 0-9, 11-18, 20-22; libcephfs advertises every bit 0..24 unless client_debug_inject_features overrides it.
gates: CEPHFS_FEATURE_MIMIC (bit 8) on the client side for the MDS bitmap to be sent
features.notes: First releases per bit (wire-protocol 3.6.1): bits 5-8 Linux v4.19 / Ceph 13.2.2; 9 v5.1 / 14.2.0; 10 never in Linux / 14.2.0; 11 v5.0 / 13.2.7, 14.2.0; 12 v5.1 / 14.2.0; 13 v5.7 / 15.2.0; 14 v5.9 / 16.2.0; 15 v6.6 / 16.2.0; 16 v6.0 / 16.2.11, 17.2.6, 18.2.0; 17 v6.1 / 16.2.11, 17.2.6, 18.2.0; 18 v6.6 / 16.2.14, 17.2.7, 18.2.0; 19 never / 17.2.8, 18.2.0; 20 v6.7 / 17.2.8, 18.2.1, 19.2.0; 21 v6.10 / 18.2.4, 19.2.0; 22 v7.1 (kernel meaning SUBVOLUME_METRICS) / 19.2.3, 20.2.0; 23 never / 19.2.3, 20.2.0; 24 never / no tag yet (main only). Kernels before v6.0 ORed each bit into byte (list index)/8 instead of bit/8, correct only while advertised bits from 8 up stay below 16 (fixed in v6.0; kclient expectations 7.1.1). CentOS Stream 8 (4.18.0-448) advertises the v6.0 set, CentOS Stream 9 (5.14.0-757) the v6.10 set. See also F-QOS-011 (metrics negotiation).

legacy_parts.note: OPEN without supported_features and metric_spec (MClientSession v1) for sessions lacking CEPHFS_FEATURE_MIMIC (bit 8). The 7.3 kernel (bits 0-9, 11-18, 20-22) and libcephfs at this commit (bits 0-24) advertise bit 8, so every OPEN they receive is v7 with the MDS bitmap and metric spec. An OPEN without them (MClientSession v1) goes only to sessions without bit 8: kernels up to v4.18 and Ceph clients up to 13.2.1.

features.name: Per-bit gated behaviour and feature names
features.summary: Which CephFS bits change MDS behaviour, which bits only steer the client, and the bit names used by mon commands and dumps.
features.description: MDS behaviour gated on the client bit: 8 MIMIC (session messages carry features, metric spec and error_string), 9 REPLY_ENCODING (versioned InodeStat/DirStat/LeaseStat), 11 LAZY_CAP_WANTED (only notable caps re-issued on stale-session resume), 13 DELEG_INO (openc_response_t create reply), 16 NOTIFY_SESSION_STATE (duplicate open answered with OPEN), 19 NEW_SNAPREALM_INFO (new snap-trace element), 21 MDS_AUTH_CAPS_CHECK (broken root_squash reporting), 22 CHARMAP (charmap gate), 24 QUARANTINE (quarantine checks and MQuarantineDisable). Bits 5-7 are release markers and bits 10, 12, 14, 15, 17, 18, 20 and 23 change nothing in the MDS. Clients test the MDS bits: the kernel 9, 12, 13, 14, 15, 17, 18, 20, 22; libcephfs 9, 10, 12, 13, 14, 17, 18, 19, 20, 23 plus metric-spec bit 16; a missing MDS bit degrades client behaviour (legacy encodings, no metrics, -EOPNOTSUPP for getvxattr, blockdiff and reclaim, 8-bit retry counters). cephfs_feature_name/cephfs_feature_from_name map bits to names (jewel .. quarantine, reserved for 0-4) for ceph fs required_client_features, ceph fs feature ls and session dumps.
features.notes: cephfs_feature_name tests "if (id > size)" and so indexes one past the name array for id 25 (wire-protocol 8). CEPHFS_FEATURE_MAX is 24. See also F-QOS-070 (quarantine bit 24). Kernel uses of two MDS bits not named above: setting an fscrypt policy (FS_IOC_SET_ENCRYPTION_POLICY) fails with -EOPNOTSUPP unless the first existing session in the kernel's session array has MDS bit 15 ALTERNATE_NAME (vet_mds_for_fscrypt stops at the first non-NULL session); on an idmapped mount a request sent to an MDS session without bit 20 HAS_OWNER_UIDGID fails with -EIO unless the module parameter enable_unsafe_idmap is set (then the client sends the idmapped fsuid/fsgid as caller and warns once). See also F-NS-064 (fscrypt), F-NS-076 (alternate_name), F-PROTO-065 (request head versions).

legacy_parts.note: MDS behaviour for sessions without bit 8 (v1 session messages, no error_string), 9 (legacy InodeStat/DirStat/LeaseStat), 11 (all caps re-issued on stale resume), 13 (raw created ino), 16 (duplicate REQUEST_OPEN dropped), 21 (broken root_squash reporting) and 22 (charmap -EPERM); client fallbacks towards an MDS without bits 9, 10, 12-15, 17-20, 23 or metric-spec bit 16. The 7.3 kernel and libcephfs both advertise bits 8, 9, 11, 13, 16, 21 and 22, so the MDS branches for sessions missing those bits are not taken by baseline peers. The branches for missing bits 19 (old snap-trace format) and 24 (request parking) stay current because the 7.3 kernel lacks both bits. The client fallbacks towards an MDS lacking a bit (legacy encodings, no metrics, -EOPNOTSUPP for getvxattr, blockdiff, reclaim and fscrypt policies, 8-bit retry counters, -EIO on idmapped mounts) are not taken because the baseline MDS advertises bits 0-24.

features.name: Feature inference for clients that send no feature bits
features.summary: Clients whose REQUEST_OPEN carries an empty bitmap (session messages below v3) get a synthesized set of bits 0..N.
features.description: Server::infer_supported_features applies the first matching rule: metadata ceph_version starting with "ceph version 12." gives bits 0-7 (LUMINOUS); another ceph_version with connection feature FS_CHANGE_ATTR (bit 59) gives 0-6 (KRAKEN); metadata kernel_version with NEW_OSDOP_ENCODING (bit 56) gives 0-7; otherwise connection FS_FILE_LAYOUT_V2 (bit 58) gives 0-5 (JEWEL); none gives an empty set. It runs at open and at reconnect when the stored set is empty, and the result is journaled with the session. Such sessions never have bit 8, 9 or 13, so they receive v1 session messages, legacy reply encodings and the raw created ino, and any required bit above the inferred range rejects them.
features.notes: Matching clients: kernels v4.13-v4.18 (luminous rule), v4.5-v4.12 (jewel rule), none before v4.5 (empty); luminous 12.x userspace; kraken 11.x and mimic 13.2.0-13.2.1 (kraken rule, they still send session v2); jewel 10.2.x (jewel rule) (kclient expectations 7.1.3). Requiring bit 8 (candidate floor F1) leaves this path unused.

legacy.note: Inference runs only when REQUEST_OPEN, or the stored session at reconnect, carries an empty CephFS bitmap. Such sessions come from kernels up to v4.18 and Ceph clients up to 13.2.1, which send session message v2. The 7.3 kernel sends a v7 REQUEST_OPEN with bits 0-9, 11-18, 20-22 and libcephfs at this commit sends bits 0-24.

features.name: required_client_features enforcement and min_compat_client
features.summary: A per-file-system bitmap in the MDSMap lists CephFS bits required from every client of that file system; the MDS rejects, denies or evicts clients that miss one.
features.description: ceph fs required_client_features <fs> add|rm <name|bit> edits the bitmap (bit 0..CEPHFS_FEATURE_MAX, name reserved refused, connected clients not checked); the deprecated ceph fs set <fs> min_compat_client <release> replaces the whole bitmap with one release-marker bit (13 octopus and later, 12 nautilus, 8 mimic, 7 luminous, 6 kraken, 5 jewel), so it cannot require anything newer than octopus. The MDS copies the bitmap when a new MDSMap changes it. REQUEST_OPEN missing a bit (after inference) gets REJECT plus a cluster-log warning (error_string "missing required features '<hex>'" only for bit-8 sessions); a reconnect missing a bit gets CLOSE (reconnect denied); on a bitmap change, once the rank is at least up:reconnect, every non-blocklisted client session missing a bit is evicted (blocklisted per mds_session_blocklist_on_evict). The test is per bit, applies to every session of the file system, and the MDS never consults the OSDMap require_min_compat_client.
gates: mon command ceph fs set <fs> min_compat_client (deprecated)
features.notes: Derived from code: v6.0+ kernels (and CentOS Stream 8/9) skip required_client_features in the MDSMap as a u64 set while it is encoded as a byte-length bitmap, so once any bit is required they misparse the rest of the map extension and usually lose max_xattr_size, which sends every buffered xattr change through a synchronous SETXATTR (kclient expectations 7.1.6). Bits 10, 19, 23 and 24 cannot be required without refusing every kernel, and bit 22 means different things to kernels and Ceph clients (7.1.7). libcephfs reports a rejection as "mds.N rejected us" and -EPERM; the kernel marks the session REJECTED and requests fail with -EACCES.

legacy_parts.note: `ceph fs set <fs> min_compat_client` and MDSMap::set_min_compat_client; feature inference before the required-bit test at open and reconnect; REJECT without error_string for sessions without bit 8. The required_client_features bitmap, its mon command and the reject, deny and evict enforcement are current. The deprecated `ceph fs set <fs> min_compat_client` (its output calls itself deprecated and points to required_client_features) is used by no baseline peer: a search of src/pybind/mgr, src/cephadm, src/python-common and rook/pkg finds only uses of the OSDMap require_min_compat_client. Inference before the test and REJECT without error_string concern only sessions without a bitmap or without bit 8 (kernels up to v4.18, Ceph up to 13.2.1).

features.name: Connection-level feature bits consulted by the client protocol
features.summary: Messenger CEPH_FEATURE_* bits negotiated per connection that select client-message encodings and a few behaviours.
features.description: The MDS messenger advertises CEPH_FEATURES_ALL. Bits consulted on client connections: FLOCK (3) - MClientCaps encoded as v1 without it; DIRLAYOUTHASH (7) - dir_layout in legacy InodeStat; CREATEPOOLID (26) - args.open.pool honoured; REPLY_CREATE_INODE (27) - raw u64 created ino; MDSENC (29) - client-chosen reconnect v3; EXPORT_PEER (37) - MClientCaps v3 import peer, and FLUSHMSG only sent to such clients; MDS_INLINE_DATA (40) - inline fields, opening an inline file without it is -EPERM, new inodes never inline; MDS_QUOTA (47) - quota in legacy InodeStat; FS_FILE_LAYOUT_V2 (58) - pool namespace, a directory with a namespaced layout gives -EIO without it; FS_BTIME = FS_CHANGE_ATTR = MSG_ADDR2 (59) - request head format and btime/change_attr; NEW_OSDOP_ENCODING (56) for feature inference. The kernel itself tests the MDS connection for FS_BTIME (legacy request head without it), MDSENC (reconnect v3) and SERVER_LUMINOUS (21; REQUEST_FLUSH_MDLOG only to such MDSs). Feature tests use masks that include incarnation bits.
features.notes: The kernel advertises bit 59 under the name MSG_ADDR2 and bit 58 under CRUSH_TUNABLES5/NEW_OSDOPREPLY_ENCODING, so a modern kernel looks like it has FS_BTIME and FS_FILE_LAYOUT_V2 (wire-protocol 3.6). The kernel advertises all transport-relevant bits except UID and OSDREPLYMUX, which the MDS requires only from mons, MDS peers, the mgr and OSDs. It also does not advertise CREATEPOOLID (26) (linux/include/linux/ceph/ceph_features.h:115, absent from :179-220) and never sets args.open.pool, so the MDS ignores that field for kernel CREATE and OPEN requests (src/mds/Server.cc:4954-4956); libcephfs advertises the bit and sends -1 or a chosen pool (src/client/Client.cc:11151, :16198). FLOCK exists since kernel 2.6.36 and EXPORT_PEER since 3.14, so no current client exercises the v1/v2 MClientCaps fallback.

legacy_parts.note: MClientCaps v1/v2 (no FLOCK/EXPORT_PEER); connection-feature field presence in the legacy InodeStat (only without bit 9); raw u64 created ino via REPLY_CREATE_INODE (only without bit 13); FLUSHMSG skipped without EXPORT_PEER; -EPERM opening an inline file, non-inline new inodes and NOINLINE/NOPOOLNS/NOQUOTA cap states without MDS_INLINE_DATA/FS_FILE_LAYOUT_V2/MDS_QUOTA; -EIO for namespaced directory layouts without FS_FILE_LAYOUT_V2; NEW_OSDOP_ENCODING, FS_CHANGE_ATTR and FS_FILE_LAYOUT_V2 in feature inference; kernel legacy request head (no FS_BTIME), reconnect v2 (no MDSENC) and suppressed FLUSH_MDLOG (no SERVER_LUMINOUS); inline data content (deprecated inline_data setting). The 7.3 kernel advertises FLOCK, DIRLAYOUTHASH, REPLY_CREATE_INODE, MDSENC, EXPORT_PEER, MDS_INLINE_DATA, MDS_QUOTA, NEW_OSDOP_ENCODING, bit 58 and bit 59, and C++ clients advertise CEPH_FEATURES_ALL, so the MDS branches for connections lacking these bits and the client fallbacks towards an MDS lacking FS_BTIME, MDSENC or SERVER_LUMINOUS are not taken by baseline peers. CREATEPOOLID is current on both sides of its test, because libcephfs advertises it and the 7.3 kernel does not. Inline data beyond CEPH_INLINE_NONE exists only after the deprecated `ceph fs set <fs> inline_data true --yes-i-really-really-mean-it`, which no mgr module, cephadm, Rook or tool sets.

features.name: Feature bit 22 numbering conflict (Ceph CHARMAP vs kernel SUBVOLUME_METRICS)
features.summary: The 7.1+ kernel and Ceph use CephFS bit 22 for different features, which changes MDS and kernel behaviour in both directions.
features.description: In this tree bit 22 is CEPHFS_FEATURE_CHARMAP (first released in 19.2.3 and 20.2.0) and there is no subvolume-metrics feature bit (libcephfs uses metric-spec bit 16). The kernel numbers CEPHFS_FEATURE_SUBVOLUME_METRICS 22 by enum position and advertises it since v7.1. The only MDS test of the bit is Server::can_handle_charmap, which fails create (O_CREAT), mkdir, symlink, link and rename into a directory with a charmap with -EPERM unless the session has bit 22 (mknod is not gated); a v7.1+ kernel therefore passes the gate although it skips the charmap optmetadata and neither normalizes nor case-folds names. In the other direction the kernel enables subvolume metrics on every OPEN whose MDS bitmap has bit 22 (the last OPEN from any rank decides) and then sends type-16 metric items, which this tree decodes.
features.notes: Derived from code, not observed: a v7.1+ kernel creates entries under the user spelling with an empty alternate_name in a directory whose libcephfs-created entries are stored folded, so names differing only in case can coexist (kclient expectations 7.1.4). Per release: 18.2.x and older and 19.2.0-19.2.2 lack bit 22; 19.2.3 and 20.2.x advertise it but send InodeStat v8 (no subvolume_id), so no type-16 items flow; this tree and 21.x send InodeStat v9 and decode type 16. Requiring bit 22 admits only v7.1+ kernels and 19.2.3+/20.2.0+ Ceph clients, with different meanings. See also F-QOS-017 (metrics side), F-NS-075 (charmap).

legacy_parts.note: The -EPERM branch of Server::can_handle_charmap for sessions without bit 22. Both baseline client families advertise bit 22 (the 7.3 kernel as SUBVOLUME_METRICS since v7.1, libcephfs as CHARMAP), so Server::can_handle_charmap never refuses them and the numbering conflict itself is current. The -EPERM refusal is reached only by sessions without bit 22: kernels before v7.1 and Ceph clients before 19.2.3 and 20.2.0.

features.name: Client generations and candidate minimum client floors
features.summary: Fact table of what representative kernel and Ceph client generations send and expect, and which fallbacks each candidate minimum generation would leave unused.
features.description: Representative generations (kclient expectations 7.1.5): Linux v4.18 (no bitmap, session v2, legacy request head, reconnect v3, legacy replies, raw created ino, caps v10, msgr1 only); v5.4 (bits 0-9, 11, 12, versioned replies); v5.10 (0-9, 11-14, openc_response_t); v5.14/v5.15 (request head v1, msgr2 opt-in); v6.6 (head v2, caps v12); v6.8 (session v7, head v3); v6.12 and 7.3 (cap_auths used); Ceph 13.2.2 (bits 0-8), 14.2.0 (0-12, reconnect v5, msgr2), 15.2.0 (0-13), 16.2.0/17.2.0 (0-15), 18.2.0 (0-19), 19.2.0 (0-21), 20.2.0 (0-23). Candidate floors and the bit that enforces them: F1 bitmap (bit 8, v4.19+, 13.2.2+), F2 Nautilus (bit 12 or 9, v5.1+, 14.2.0+), F3 Octopus (bit 13, v5.7+, 15.2.0+), F4 versioned head (bit 16 or 17, v6.0+/v6.1+), F5 32-bit retry/forward (bit 18, v6.6+), F6 owner uid/gid (bit 20, v6.7+), F7 client-side MDS cap checks (bit 21, v6.10+). Not removed by any floor: msgr1 for kernels mounted without ms_mode (no CephFS bit reveals msgr2 capability; mount.ceph passes ms_mode=prefer-crc for the new device syntax since 17.2.0), single-message reconnect v3 (every kernel v4.8-7.3, the current kernel's format), the old snap-trace format (no kernel sets bit 19, so it is the current kernel's format), session open v4 (CentOS Stream 9 with bit 21), and bits no kernel has (10, 19, 23, 24).
features.notes: Enterprise kernels backport CephFS changes and do not follow their base version: CentOS Stream 8 4.18.0-448.el8 behaves like upstream v6.0 for feature bits, CentOS Stream 9 5.14.0-757.el9 like v6.10; no other distribution kernel was examined. A non-empty required_client_features also triggers the kernel MDSMap mis-skip described in F-PROTO-023.

legacy_parts.note: Rows for Linux v4.18-v6.12, CentOS Stream 8/9 and Ceph 13.2.2-20.2.0; candidate floors F1-F7 with the fallbacks each would leave unused; the 'not removed by any floor' items msgr1 and session open v4 (CentOS Stream 9). Of the generations in the table only the 7.3 kernel and Ceph clients at this commit are baseline peers. The facts that stay current are those of the 7.3 kernel: session open v7, head v3 in message v6, single-message reconnect v3, the old snap-trace format and the absence of bits 10, 19, 23 and 24. The older Linux, CentOS Stream 8/9 and Ceph 13.2.2-20.2.0 rows, the candidate floors F1-F7, session open v4 (CentOS Stream 9) and msgr1 concern clients or mount configurations outside the baseline.

features.name: Session state machine
features.summary: Every client holds one session per rank, in one of six MDS-side states, before requests, caps or leases are accepted.
features.description: States: closed (0), opening (1, journaling open), open (2), closing (3, journaling close), stale (4), killing (5), plus an orthogonal importing_count for sessions force-opened on behalf of a client. Every state change increments state_seq and asynchronous completions become no-ops if it changed. Transitions: closed to opening on a valid REQUEST_OPEN or force open; opening to open when ESession(open) is safe; open to stale in idle detection; stale to open on REQUEST_RENEWCAPS; open/stale/opening to closing on REQUEST_CLOSE with matching seq; open/stale/opening (not importing) to killing on kill_session; closing/killing to closed and removal when the close is journaled; closing/killing to opening on a force open by import or rejoin. Sessions loaded from RADOS or created by journal replay start in open. Client-side states differ: the kernel has NEW, OPENING, OPEN, HUNG, CLOSING, CLOSED, RESTARTING, RECONNECTING, REJECTED; libcephfs OPENING, OPEN, CLOSING, CLOSED, STALE, REJECTED, and keeps sending requests on a STALE session.
features.notes: REQUEST_CLOSE is accepted in opening; the later open completion still consumes its projected version but makes no state change and sends no OPEN (sessions 3.2).

features.name: Session open handshake (REQUEST_OPEN, journaled open, OPEN)
features.summary: A client opens a session per rank with REQUEST_OPEN; the MDS validates it, journals the open and only then replies OPEN.
features.description: The kernel sends REQUEST_OPEN as MClientSession v7 with exactly four metadata keys (hostname, kernel_version, entity_id, root), its feature bitmap, a metric spec for types 0-16, flags 0, an empty cap_auths vector and oldest_client_tid; libcephfs sends v7 with its metadata, all feature bits and CEPHFS_METRIC_FEATURES_ALL. On acceptance the MDS adds the session to the SessionMap, projects a new SessionMap version, sets opening, submits ESession(open, client_metadata, auth_name) and flushes the log; after the commit it sets open, registers the session with the dmClock scheduler and MetricsHandler, and sends OPEN with seq 0, supported_features and metric_spec (MIMIC clients only) and cap_auths, followed by FORCE_RO if the cache is read-only. REQUEST_OPEN is queued until the rank is at least up:clientreplay. The kernel queues requests for that rank until OPEN; libcephfs sends an immediate REQUEST_RENEWCAPS after OPEN and opens sessions to the rank's export targets.
features.notes: Open completes after one journal flush (sessions 7, timing summary). Session-open message versions received from clients: v2 (kernels up to v4.18, Ceph up to 13.2.1), v3 (v4.19-v5.8, 13.2.2-14.x), v4 (v5.9-v6.7, CentOS Stream 8 and 9, 15.2.0-15.2.15, 16.2.0-16.2.6), v5 (15.2.16+, 16.2.7+, 17.2.x, 18.2.0-18.2.2), v7 (v6.8+, 18.2.4, 19.2.0+) (kclient expectations 7.1.2). The kernel never writes stamp, max_caps or max_leases in its session head; the MDS does not read them. See also F-STORE-028 (ESession events).

legacy_parts.note: Decoding REQUEST_OPEN messages that end at v2-v5 (no cap_auths, no oldest_client_tid; v2 also without a bitmap); OPEN encoded as v1 for sessions without bit 8. The 7.3 kernel sends REQUEST_OPEN as MClientSession v7 and libcephfs at this commit encodes it as v7. Versions v2-v5 come only from older clients: v2 from kernels up to v4.18 and Ceph up to 13.2.1, v3 from kernels v4.19-v5.8, v4 from kernels v5.9-v6.7 and CentOS Stream 8 and 9, and v3-v5 from Ceph releases before 18.2.4 and 19.2.0. OPEN without supported_features and metric_spec goes only to sessions without bit 8.

features.name: Session open admission checks and rejection reasons
features.summary: The ordered checks the MDS applies to REQUEST_OPEN, and the REJECT reasons clients can see.
features.description: Before any op: no session on the connection gives REJECT "sessionless"; a session lacking MAY_READ caps for this rank's fs_name gives REJECT naming the file system (both for every session op, not only open). For REQUEST_OPEN, in order: MDSMap flag refuse_client_session (REJECT with an explanatory error_string); session closing (wait for the journal and retry); session opening/open/stale/killing or sessions being terminated (drop, or duplicate-open OPEN, F-PROTO-037); rank stopping (drop); store client_metadata; address in the OSD blocklist (REJECT with SESSION_BLOCKLISTED); infer features if none; missing required features (REJECT); root_squash caps without bit 21 (flagged, not rejected); metadata root empty or not starting with "/" (REJECT "invalue root", literal typo) or not allowed by the cap path (REJECT "non-allowable root"); metadata uuid already used by another session (REJECT "duplicated session uuid"); otherwise accept. Rejections of the last rows also emit cluster-log warnings and a debug log line with status REJECTED.
gates: MDSMap flag refuse_client_session (ceph fs set <fs> refuse_client_session true)
features.notes: With refuse_client_session set even a duplicate REQUEST_OPEN from an open session gets REJECT, because the flag is checked before the state (sessions 8). libcephfs fails the mount with -EACCES before opening a session when the MDSMap has the flag. The monitor requires refuse_client_session before fs rename. Connection-level refusals (cephx failure, unparsable MDS caps) never reach this code. See also F-ADM-017 (mount root and reclaim auth checks).

legacy_parts.note: The infer_supported_features step; flagging root_squash sessions without bit 21 as broken. Feature inference runs only for REQUEST_OPEN without a bitmap, which kernels up to v4.18 and Ceph up to 13.2.1 send. The broken-root_squash flag, reported as MDS_HEALTH_CLIENTS_BROKEN_ROOTSQUASH, applies only to sessions without bit 21 (kernels before v6.10, Ceph before 18.2.4 and 19.2.0). The 7.3 kernel and libcephfs send a bitmap that contains bit 21.

features.name: REJECT encoding and blocklist signalling to clients
features.summary: How a refused or blocklisted client learns about it from CEPH_SESSION_REJECT, and what each client does next.
features.description: REJECT messages built by send_reject_message carry metadata error_string only for clients that advertised MIMIC; the sessionless, no-fs-caps and refuse_client_session REJECTs always carry it (so they are encoded as v7). For a blocklisted address the MDS sets flags = SESSION_BLOCKLISTED (1) and error_string "blocklisted (blacklisted)". A v1-encoded REJECT (pre-mimic client) has neither flags nor error_string. The kernel marks itself blocklisted from the flag (session message v5+) or from an error_string containing "blacklisted" (v3/v4 only), marks the session REJECTED, fails later requests to that rank with -EACCES, and with recover_session=clean force-reconnects with a new address nonce; it WARNs on a REJECT that arrives when the session is neither OPENING nor RECONNECTING. libcephfs logs error_string, closes the session with -EPERM and ignores flags; requests to a REJECTED rank fail with -EPERM.
gates: client bit CEPHFS_FEATURE_MIMIC (8) for error_string and flags
features.notes: The C++ code comment states the kernel depends on the substring "blacklisted"; current kernels receive v7 REJECTs and use the flag only. A sessionless REJECT to a RENEWCAPS of an OPEN kernel session trips the kernel WARN_ON and marks the session REJECTED (kclient expectations 3.4.3). See also F-PROTO-052 (blocklist-driven kill).

legacy_parts.note: v1 REJECT for sessions without bit 8; the '(blacklisted)' substring in the blocklist error_string; the kernel's blocklist-marker scan of v3/v4 session metadata. Baseline clients advertise bit 8 and receive REJECT as v7 with flags and error_string; the 7.3 kernel takes blocklisting from the flag of v5+ messages and libcephfs logs error_string. A REJECT without flags or error_string goes only to sessions without bit 8, and in a v7 REJECT the 'blacklisted' substring of error_string is read only by kernels v5.4-v5.15, because flag decoding arrived with kernel commit e1c9788cb397 in v5.16. The kernel's error_string scan of v3/v4 session messages applies only to MDS releases that sent MClientSession v3 or v4.

features.name: MClientSession encoding and the ops the MDS sends
features.summary: Field layout of MClientSession v1-v7 and which session ops the MDS sends to clients.
features.description: Payload: raw ceph_mds_session_head (28 bytes: u32 op, u64 seq, ceph_timespec stamp, u32 max_caps, u32 max_leases); v2 map<string,string> metadata; v3 feature_bitset_t supported_features; v4 metric_spec_t; v5 u32 flags; v6 vector<MDSCapAuth> cap_auths; v7 u64 oldest_client_tid (default UINT64_MAX = do not trim). The encoder writes v1 (head only) when metadata and supported_features are both empty, otherwise v7. MDS-to-client ops: OPEN (1), CLOSE (3), RENEWCAPS (5), STALE (6), RECALL_STATE (7, head.max_caps = new cap limit; owned by cap recall), FLUSHMSG (8), FORCE_RO (10), REJECT (11); client-to-MDS ops: REQUEST_OPEN (0), REQUEST_CLOSE (2), REQUEST_RENEWCAPS (4), FLUSHMSG_ACK (9), REQUEST_FLUSH_MDLOG (12). MDS-originated messages are therefore v1 unless they carry error_string or are an OPEN to a MIMIC client. libcephfs ceph_abort()s on any received op other than the eight MDS ops; the kernel WARNs. Any session message resets the kernel s_ttl and moves a HUNG session back to OPEN.
features.notes: The head stamp is read by neither the MDS, libcephfs nor the kernel handle_session (search only). The kernel decodes by version: v3/v4 scan metadata for the blocklist marker, v5+ skip metadata and read flags, it reads only the first 64 feature bits, skips metric_spec, parses cap_auths only on OPEN and ignores oldest_client_tid.

legacy_parts.note: Decoding client-sent MClientSession versions 2-5; the kernel's version-3/4 metadata scan for the blocklist marker. Baseline clients send session messages as v1-format head-only messages (kernel ceph_create_session_msg, libcephfs messages without metadata) or as v7, and the MDS sends v1 or v7, so these encodings are current. Client messages that end at v2-v5 come only from kernels up to v6.7, CentOS Stream 8 and 9 and Ceph releases before 18.2.4 and 19.2.0. The kernel's v3/v4 decode path applies only to MDS releases that sent those versions.

features.name: Session op dispatch and rank-state gating
features.summary: Which session ops the MDS handles in which rank state, and what each client op does.
features.description: REQUEST_RENEWCAPS is handled in any rank state; REQUEST_CLOSE waits until the rank is up:active; REQUEST_OPEN, FLUSHMSG_ACK and REQUEST_FLUSH_MDLOG wait until up:clientreplay (CREATING and STARTING are numerically below REPLAY, so such comparisons also hold for them). Per op: REQUEST_OPEN validates and journals an open; REQUEST_RENEWCAPS renews (open or stale sessions only); REQUEST_CLOSE closes when seq equals push_seq; FLUSHMSG_ACK completes flush waiters with key <= seq; REQUEST_FLUSH_MDLOG flushes the log when active, without reply; any other value gets REJECT and eviction. Every client message of any type that reaches the MDS dispatcher updates Session::last_seen, which idle detection uses as liveness.

features.name: Unknown session op handling
features.summary: A session op the MDS does not handle (including MDS-to-client ops sent by a client) gets REJECT and the client is evicted and blocklisted.
features.description: Server::handle_client_session sends a v1 REJECT (no error_string), logs at derr and calls evict_client with blocklist=true regardless of mds_session_blocklist_on_evict. Unmodified kernel and libcephfs clients only send the five client ops.
features.notes: Old kernels gate their newer ops on MDS features for this reason: REQUEST_FLUSH_MDLOG only to SERVER_LUMINOUS peers ("Pre-luminous MDS crashes when it sees an unknown session request"), GETVXATTR only with bit 17 (kclient expectations 8).

features.name: Client metadata capture and use
features.summary: The key/value metadata a client sends at open, which keys the MDS interprets, and which consumers read it back.
features.description: client_metadata_t = kv map + feature bitset + metric spec, stored on the session and journaled with it. Kernel keys: hostname, kernel_version, entity_id, root (server path or "/"). libcephfs keys: hostname, pid, entity_id, root (at mount; absent on sessions opened before mount by ceph_start_reclaim), ceph_version, ceph_sha1, client_metadata config pairs, uuid (ceph_set_uuid), timeout (ceph_set_session_timeout); ceph-fuse adds mount_point. The MDS uses root (open-time path check, dmClock volume id), uuid (duplicate check, reclaim lookup), timeout (idle and reconnect handling), ceph_version/kernel_version (feature inference) and hostname (session human name); other keys are only shown in session ls and matched by client_metadata.<key> filters. On force open the kv keys are merged without overwriting and features/metric spec replaced.
features.notes: mgr stats requires client_metadata.hostname and client_metadata.root in client ls output (KeyError otherwise) and parses metric_spec.metric_flags.feature_bits; volumes evicts by client_metadata.root and auth_name; the dashboard reads ceph_version, kernel_version, hostname and root (sessions 7).

legacy_parts.note: Use of the ceph_version and kernel_version metadata keys for feature inference. The MDS reads ceph_version and kernel_version only in infer_supported_features, which runs only for sessions without a feature bitmap (kernels up to v4.18, Ceph up to 13.2.1). Baseline clients still send these keys and the dashboard shows them, but they always send a bitmap.

features.name: Duplicate REQUEST_OPEN answered with OPEN (NOTIFY_SESSION_STATE)
features.summary: A client that re-sends REQUEST_OPEN on a session the MDS already has open gets a fresh OPEN if it advertises bit 16; otherwise the request is dropped.
features.description: If the duplicate REQUEST_OPEN advertises CEPHFS_FEATURE_NOTIFY_SESSION_STATE, the session is open and the rank is not stopping, the MDS re-sends OPEN with seq = current push_seq, supported_features (if the stored features have MIMIC) and cap_auths but no metric_spec, followed by FORCE_RO if read-only; otherwise it drops the message. Both clients copy a non-zero OPEN seq into their session seq when theirs is 0 (libcephfs only if its session was not already open), which resynchronizes the push-seq counter after a client-side session re-init; both overwrite their copy of the MDS feature bits on every OPEN.
gates: client bit CEPHFS_FEATURE_NOTIFY_SESSION_STATE (16): Linux v6.0+, Ceph 16.2.11, 17.2.6, 18.2.0+
features.notes: Because this OPEN has no metric_spec and libcephfs copies both fields on every OPEN, it clears libcephfs's copy of the MDS metric spec, which stops spec-gated metric types including subvolume metrics (derived from code; wire-protocol 8). A client without bit 16 that lost the first OPEN waits.

legacy_parts.note: Silent drop of a duplicate REQUEST_OPEN from sessions without bit 16; OPEN without supported_features for sessions without bit 8. The 7.3 kernel and libcephfs at this commit advertise bits 16 and 8, so a duplicate REQUEST_OPEN from them is answered with OPEN carrying supported_features. Dropping the duplicate applies only to clients without bit 16 (kernels before v6.0, Ceph before 16.2.11, 17.2.6 and 18.2.0), and omitting supported_features only to sessions without bit 8.

features.name: FORCE_RO: read-only MDS notification
features.summary: When the MDS metadata cache is (or turns) read-only it tells every client session, and clients then refuse new write caps locally.
features.description: Server::force_clients_readonly sends CEPH_SESSION_FORCE_RO (v1) to every client session in open or stale when MDCache::force_readonly runs, and new and reconnected sessions get FORCE_RO right after OPEN. The kernel sets s_readonly and later cap waits needing Fw or Fx on that session's auth cap fail with -EROFS; libcephfs sets session->readonly and get_caps(Fw) on an inode whose auth cap is on that session returns -EROFS. A read-only rank also denies reconnects with CLOSE and rejects W-bit requests with -EROFS.
features.notes: The read-only transition itself (write errors, mds_action_on_write_error) is owned by 06-journal-and-storage. See also F-STORE-100, F-ADM-042.

features.name: FLUSHMSG / FLUSHMSG_ACK session barrier
features.summary: The MDS can make sure a client has processed every counted message sent so far, and flushed its pending cap releases, before it proceeds.
features.description: Server::flush_session sends CEPH_SESSION_FLUSHMSG with seq = the session push_seq to open sessions whose connection has EXPORT_PEER and registers a waiter; the waiter completes on FLUSHMSG_ACK with seq >= that value, when the session goes stale, or when it is closed. Both clients first send their queued MClientCapRelease and then answer FLUSHMSG_ACK with the same seq. Users: subtree export (clients have seen every cap message before the export proceeds), the cross-MDS rename peer that exports the renamed inode, and the cache drop recall loop.
gates: connection feature EXPORT_PEER (37) on the client connection

legacy_parts.note: flush_session returning early for connections without EXPORT_PEER. Both baseline client families negotiate EXPORT_PEER (bit 37), so every open baseline session receives FLUSHMSG. Skipping the barrier for connections without EXPORT_PEER applies only to clients older than Linux 3.14 and Ceph v0.75.

features.name: REQUEST_FLUSH_MDLOG and the client sync paths
features.summary: Clients ask the MDS to flush its journal so that unsafe requests become safe sooner; fsync, syncfs, unmount and every NFS commit or setattr through Ganesha depend on it.
features.description: CEPH_SESSION_REQUEST_FLUSH_MDLOG (op 12, seq = the client session seq) makes the MDS call mdlog->flush() when the rank is active; there is no reply. The kernel sends it only to MDSs whose connection has SERVER_LUMINOUS: from fsync when the inode (or a directory's dir ops) has unsafe requests, to every session holding those plus the auth-cap session; from syncfs to each session with outstanding write requests; to all sessions at unmount and manual reset. fsync then waits for the safe replies of the last unsafe dir op and inode op and, if non-file metadata was dirty, for flush acks. libcephfs _fsync flushes data, sends a FLAG_SYNC cap flush, sends FLUSH_MDLOG to the ranks holding unsafe requests plus the auth rank, and waits for the newest unsafe request's safe reply and the FLUSH_ACK. FSAL_CEPH turns NFS COMMIT, stable WRITEs, ALLOCATE/DEALLOCATE and every SETATTR into ceph_ll_sync_inode/ceph_ll_fsync, so the MDS log-flush latency bounds those NFS operations.
gates: connection feature SERVER_LUMINOUS (21) on the MDS connection (kernel and libcephfs send the op only then)
features.notes: The cap-flush side of fsync (FLAG_SYNC, FLUSH_ACK) is owned by 03-caps-leases-and-locking. Derived from code: every NFS SETATTR through Ganesha waits for the MDS journal (libcephfs-fuse-ganesha 8). The op is ignored in every rank state other than up:active (including up:clientreplay). The kernel waits with wait_for_completion_timeout(r_timeout) and returns -EIO on expiry, but r_timeout is 0 (no timeout) for ordinary requests, so fsync waits until the safe reply (linux/fs/ceph/caps.c:2502-2512). See also F-NS-016 (fsync contract), F-STORE-008 (group commit).

features.name: Force-opened sessions (imports, rejoin, cross-MDS rename)
features.summary: A rank can open a session on behalf of a client that never sent REQUEST_OPEN to it, when it imports caps for that client; the client receives an unsolicited OPEN.
features.description: prepare_force_open_sessions drops blocklisted clients, gets or adds a session without connection, projects a SessionMap version, moves closed/closing/killing sessions to opening (kv metadata merged without overwriting, features and metric spec replaced) and increments importing_count; the caller journals the projected version in EImportStart, ESessions or the rename leader's EUpdate. After the journal commit, sessions still at the captured state_seq become open, are registered with metrics and dmClock, and receive OPEN (queued in preopen_out_queue until the client connects) and FORCE_RO if needed. An importing session is not closed by REQUEST_CLOSE, kill_session or idle eviction; on import failure the sessions the client never opened itself are closed again. Callers: subtree and cap import, rejoin, cross-rank rename.
features.notes: The kernel opens sessions to a laggy rank's export targets and sends a reconnect to export targets in up:reconnect for which it has no session (kclient expectations 3.15). REQUEST_CLOSE on an importing session is dropped silently and the client resends it only when another counted message arrives (sessions 8). See also F-MULTI-017 (import), F-CLU-089 (rejoin), F-NS-057 (cross-rank rename).

features.name: Cap renewal (REQUEST_RENEWCAPS / RENEWCAPS)
features.summary: Clients periodically renew their session; caps and dentry leases are trusted by the client only while renewals are answered.
features.description: The client sends REQUEST_RENEWCAPS with seq = ++renew_seq. The MDS handles it in any rank state, but only for open or stale sessions: touch_session (last_cap_renew = now), a stale session goes back to open with Locker::resume_stale_caps, completed requests are trimmed by oldest_client_tid, and RENEWCAPS echoing the seq is sent immediately. The kernel renews every session_timeout/4 (15 s by default) and only to ranks in up:reconnect or later, treats caps as valid until renew_requested + session_timeout and accepts RENEWCAPS only with seq == s_renew_seq; its RENEWCAPS is a full v7 message carrying metadata and oldest_client_tid. libcephfs renews when more than session_timeout/3 elapsed and only to ranks in up:rejoin or later; its v1 RENEWCAPS carries no oldest_client_tid.
gates: MDSMap session_timeout (default 60 s, minimum 30; ceph fs set <fs> session_timeout)
features.notes: Completed-request trimming for libcephfs therefore relies only on MClientRequest.head.oldest_client_tid; the table itself is owned by 04-namespace-and-posix-operations. A cap is valid in the kernel only while cap_gen equals s_cap_gen and jiffies < s_cap_ttl; libcephfs Inode::cap_is_valid applies the same rule.

features.name: Stale session detection and the STALE message
features.summary: A session that has not renewed for session_timeout is marked stale, its caps are invalidated, and the client is told with CEPH_SESSION_STALE.
features.description: Every mds_tick_interval (5 s) in clientreplay, active or stopping, find_idle_sessions uses cutoff = messenger dispatch-queue max age + session_timeout; it does nothing in a tick if the MDS itself cleared its laggy state less than cutoff ago. It walks open sessions in renewal LRU order; a later last_seen (any message) counts as liveness. Sessions past cutoff (and not handled by the autoclose, deferred-stale or timeout rules) become stale: Locker::revoke_stale_caps increments Session::cap_gen (invalidating every cap of the session) and forcibly completes in-flight revocations without write bits; if that succeeded the leases are removed, flush waiters released and STALE sent; if a revocation including write bits was pending the client is evicted instead. Clients answer STALE by bumping their cap generation, setting cap_ttl to now - 1 and sending REQUEST_RENEWCAPS; RENEWCAPS then resets caps of older generations to PIN and the MDS re-issues caps in resume_stale_caps.
features.notes: The LRU order is approximate because reconnect updates last_cap_renew without reordering (sessions 3.6). Stale caps are revoked without waiting for an ack when another client needs them; revoking write caps from a stale session evicts it (cap semantics owned by 03-caps-leases-and-locking). libcephfs keeps sending requests on a STALE session. See also F-CAPS-030 (cap side of stale sessions).

features.name: Deferred stale marking for quiet sessions (mds_defer_session_stale)
features.summary: With the default configuration a silent session is marked stale only while the MDS is revoking caps from it or waiting for a flush from it.
features.description: When mds_defer_session_stale (dev option, default true) is set, find_idle_sessions skips a session past the stale cutoff that has no flush waiters and from which the Locker is not revoking any caps. Such a session keeps its caps until it either becomes involved in a revocation (then it goes stale or, with timeout metadata, is evicted) or reaches session_autoclose.

features.name: Session autoclose eviction
features.summary: A session silent for session_autoclose is evicted (blocklisted by default) without going through the stale state.
features.description: In find_idle_sessions an open session whose silence span reached session_autoclose (default 300 s) is put on laggy_clients; this check runs before the custom timeout check, so it also bounds sessions with a larger or infinite timeout. Stale sessions are evicted once now - last_cap_renew >= dispatch-queue max age + session_autoclose. Each laggy client that is not importing gets a cluster-log warning "evicting unresponsive client <name>, after <span> seconds" and is evicted with blocklisting if mds_session_blocklist_on_timeout (default true), otherwise killed. The kernel marks its session HUNG (client-side bookkeeping only) when no session message arrived for session_autoclose.

features.name: Per-session timeout metadata
features.summary: A client can set session metadata "timeout" so that its session is never marked stale and is evicted only by its own timeout or by autoclose; NFS-Ganesha always sets it.
features.description: libcephfs ceph_set_session_timeout(T) adds metadata timeout=T before the session opens (FSAL_CEPH always sends 300); the admin command session config <id> timeout [<value>] sets or removes it on any session. In find_idle_sessions it applies only after the autoclose check and, with mds_defer_session_stale, only when the MDS is revoking caps from or waiting for a flush from the session: such a session is never marked stale and is evicted directly once silent for dispatch-queue max age + T (T = 0: never by this rule). A timeout session that does not reconnect after a failover is kept in client_reclaim_gather instead of being evicted at the end of the reconnect window. The kernel never sends the key.
features.notes: Derived from code: with the default session_autoclose of 300 s the timeout=300 cutoff is never reached, so a silent Ganesha session from which the MDS revokes caps is never marked STALE and is evicted at autoclose, while an ordinary client in that situation goes STALE after session_timeout (libcephfs-fuse-ganesha 3.16.3). session config changes are not persisted until the session is written for another reason. See also F-ADM-039 (session config command).

features.name: Eviction deferral while OSDs are laggy
features.summary: Optionally, the MDS skips evicting unresponsive clients while the OSDMap shows laggy OSDs, and reports them instead.
