features.description: If defer_client_eviction_on_laggy_osds (default false) is set, the OSDMap has any laggy OSD and laggy_clients is non-empty, find_idle_sessions returns without evicting; the set is kept for the MDS_CLIENTS_LAGGY health warning until the next tick clears it. The same deferral applies to cap-revoke non-responder eviction.
features.notes: See also F-ADM-080 (MDS_CLIENTS_LAGGY).

features.name: Cap-revoke non-responder eviction
features.summary: Optionally, a client that does not acknowledge a cap revocation within a timeout is evicted.
features.description: With mds_cap_revoke_eviction_timeout set (default 0 = disabled), every tick the clients returned by Locker::get_late_revoking_clients for that timeout are evicted (blocklisted per mds_session_blocklist_on_evict) and perf counter cap_revoke_eviction is incremented; the laggy-OSD deferral applies. Not answering RECALL_STATE never evicts a client; only an unanswered revoke can, and only with this option.
features.notes: Ganesha delegations can hold a revoke un-acked up to the delegation timeout (F-PROTO-102). See also F-CAPS-031 (late revocation tracking).

features.name: Client-initiated close with push-sequence handshake
features.summary: A client closes its session with REQUEST_CLOSE carrying its count of received counted messages; the MDS journals the close and answers CLOSE.
features.description: REQUEST_CLOSE is handled once the rank is up:active. It is dropped if the session is closed, closing, killing or importing, dropped silently if seq < push_seq and dropped with a cluster-log warning "incorrect push seq" if seq > push_seq; with seq == push_seq journal_close_session sets closing, journals ESession(close) with the prealloc inodes to free and delegated inodes to purge, flushes the log, kills the session's in-flight requests and releases flush waiters. After the commit the MDS removes all caps and leases of the client, marks the connection disposable, sends CLOSE and removes the session. Both clients re-send REQUEST_CLOSE with the new count whenever a counted message arrives while closing. The kernel unmount waits up to mount_timeout for CLOSE, then tears sessions down locally; libcephfs waits client_shutdown_timeout (30 s) and then treats them as closed with -ETIMEDOUT. The kernel manual reset (debugfs) sends REQUEST_CLOSE, waits 100 ms and tears down locally.
features.notes: libcephfs ceph_set_uuid closes every session and can stall up to client_shutdown_timeout while a rank is held in clientreplay, because REQUEST_CLOSE waits for up:active (libcephfs-fuse-ganesha 8). The prealloc and purge bookkeeping of the close is owned by 06-journal-and-storage.

features.name: Counted messages and the session push sequence
features.summary: Both sides count the cap, lease, snap and quota messages the MDS sends on a session; the count gates REQUEST_CLOSE and FLUSHMSG.
features.description: The MDS sends MClientCaps, MClientLease, MClientSnap, MClientQuota and (only to clients with bit 24) MQuarantineDisable through send_message_client_counted, which increments Session::cap_push_seq. The kernel increments s_seq for every received CAPS, SNAP, LEASE and QUOTA message before decoding it (malformed or unmount-dropped ones are counted too); libcephfs Client::got_mds_push counts caps (all ops, including messages for unknown inodes), lease, snap and quota messages received on the session's current connection. Replies, forwards and session messages are not counted. The count is not persisted: both sides restart at 0 on reconnect (kernel s_seq = 0 in send_mds_reconnect, new or cleared Session on the MDS).
features.notes: Observed mismatch in this tree (derived from code, not verified by test): libcephfs advertises bit 24 but Client::handle_quarantine_disable does not call got_mds_push, so after one MQuarantineDisable its REQUEST_CLOSE carries a seq below push_seq and is dropped until client_shutdown_timeout (sessions 8, wire-protocol 8). The kernel does not advertise bit 24.

features.name: Client eviction: OSD blocklist, epoch barrier and session kill
features.summary: Evicting a client blocklists its address through the monitor, waits for the resulting OSDMap, raises the OSD epoch barrier and kills the session without sending CLOSE.
features.description: MDSRank::evict_client refuses while the rank replays ("MDS is replaying log"), logs "Evicting (and blocklisting) client session <id>" and, with blocklisting, sends the mon command osd blocklist add <addr> (no expiry argument, so mon_osd_blocklist_default_expire, 1 h); when the command completes (its result is ignored) it waits for the latest OSDMap, sets the MDS OSD epoch barrier to that epoch and calls kill_session. kill_session journals ESession(close) with state killing for opening/open/stale sessions that are not importing; after the commit the connection is marked down without a CLOSE message and caps are removed with the kill flag (an inode is flagged NEEDSRECOVER if the client had a writable range). The barrier goes out in later MClientCaps so other clients wait for that OSDMap before doing I/O. Triggers: autoclose and timeout eviction, reconnect timeout, stale write-cap revocation, cap-revoke timeout, missing required features, admin session evict/kill and client evict, reclaim RESET, oversized session metadata, unknown session op, last rank stopping. Clients learn of it through a peer reset, a REJECT with SESSION_BLOCKLISTED on reopen, or -EBLOCKLISTED from OSDs: libcephfs then aborts every request with -EBLOCKLISTED and force-closes all sessions; the kernel recovers only with recover_session=clean.
features.notes: If the blocklist command failed the session is still killed after waiting for the latest OSDMap; if the session disappears meanwhile on_killed still completes (sessions 8). The OSD epoch barrier mechanism is owned by 06-journal-and-storage; libcephfs with client_reconnect_stale auto-recovers from blocklisting at most every 30 minutes with a new messenger address. The mon command is {"prefix":"osd blocklist","blocklistop":"add","addr":"<session addr>"}; it requires the osd blocklist mon cap that profile mds grants. Killing after the blocklist is in the MDS's OSDMap means size recovery of NEEDSRECOVER inodes starts only after the client is fenced. session kill is synchronous. mgr volumes and the dashboard rely on the blocklist side effect of session evict. See also F-ADM-038 (admin commands), F-STORE-098 (epoch barrier).

features.name: OSDMap blocklist-driven session kill
features.summary: Client sessions whose address appears in the OSD blocklist (added by anyone) are killed when the MDS sees the new OSDMap.
features.description: Outside replay, MDSRankDispatcher::handle_osd_map takes the newly blocklisted addresses from the Objecter and MDSRank::apply_blocklist runs Server::apply_blocklist, which kills every client session (MDS peers are skipped) whose address is blocklisted in the current OSDMap, and sets the OSD epoch barrier if anything was killed. MDSRank::reconnect_start applies the full current blocklist before the reconnect phase, and a blocklisted address gets REJECT at open.
features.notes: Blocklisting by anyone therefore closes the client's sessions on every rank. Force-open (rejoin, import, cross-rank rename) skips blocklisted clients, and a session open from a blocklisted address gets REJECT with SESSION_BLOCKLISTED (F-PROTO-030).

features.name: Eviction of sessions with oversized metadata
features.summary: A session whose encoded state grows beyond mds_session_metadata_threshold is evicted when the SessionMap is saved.
features.description: At SessionMap save, sessions whose encoded session_info_t (mostly completed_requests) is at least mds_session_metadata_threshold (16 MiB) are skipped and evicted (blocklisted per mds_session_blocklist_on_evict); perf counter mdthresh_evicted counts them. The typical cause is a client that does not advance oldest_client_tid; the MDS warns earlier with "does not advance its oldest_client_tid" and health MDS_CLIENT_OLDEST_TID.
features.notes: libcephfs never transmits oldest_client_tid in RENEWCAPS, so a long-outstanding non-SETFILELOCK request pins its table (libcephfs-fuse-ganesha 8). Counter: mds_sessions.mdthresh_evicted. See also F-STORE-075 (SessionMap object), F-NS-012.

features.name: Session termination at rank shutdown
features.summary: A stopping rank closes every client session; when it is the last in rank it evicts them instead.
features.description: Server::terminate_sessions, driven by MDCache::shutdown_pass while unclosed sessions remain, journals a close (closing) for every client session not already closing, killing or closed, so clients receive CLOSE. When the stopping rank is the only in rank, MDSRank::stopping_start first evicts every client session (blocklisting per mds_session_blocklist_on_evict), so the clients of a file system being shut down are blocklisted rather than closed.
features.notes: The up:stopping state itself is owned by 01-cluster-membership-and-ha. The eviction trigger is "the only rank in" (get_num_in_mds() == 1, for example `fs set down true` or max_mds reduced to 0), not specifically rank 0; clients must remount after the file system is brought back. See also F-CLU-102 (stopping).

features.group: MDS failover reconnect and NFS-Ganesha reclaim
features.name: Reconnect trigger and client-side ordering
features.summary: When a rank is taken over by a new daemon, clients replay unsafe requests, resend unanswered ones, re-send revoked cap flushes and then describe all their caps in MClientReconnect, in that order on the new connection.
features.description: The MDS enters up:reconnect with MDSRank::reconnect_start: it applies the OSD blocklist, puts every open session (all sessions loaded or replayed are open) into client_reconnect_gather, marks them reconnecting and sets last_cap_renew = now. The kernel notices the rank's new address in the MDSMap, closes the connection, marks the session RESTARTING and, once the rank state is up:reconnect or later, resets s_seq to 0, bumps the cap generation, drops queued cap releases and delegated inodes, trims the dcache, re-sends unsafe requests with REPLAY, re-sends requests that were sent but not answered (as retries without releases), re-sends flushes of revoked flushing caps with seq = issue_seq = mseq = 0, and finally sends MClientReconnect. libcephfs reconnects when the rank state becomes exactly up:reconnect, in the same order. After the rank becomes active, clients kick waiting requests and in-flight cap flushes and reset requested max_size.
features.notes: libcephfs closes the session and drops caps (dirty metadata lost) if it sees the rank jump from below up:reconnect to beyond it (libcephfs-fuse-ganesha 8). The kernel also sends a reconnect to export targets in up:reconnect for which it has no session. See also F-CLU-080 (reconnect window and timeout).

features.group: MDS failover reconnect and NFS-Ganesha reclaim
features.name: MClientReconnect encodings (v1 to v5, multi-message)
features.summary: Layout of the reconnect message that carries every cap, realm and file lock a client holds from a rank.
features.description: The whole payload is in the data segment. v4/v5 (compat 4): map<inodeno_t, cap_reconnect_t> caps, vector<snaprealm_reconnect_t> realms, v5 bool more (another reconnect message follows). cap_reconnect_t = ENCODE_START(2,1) {string path, raw 36-byte ceph_mds_cap_reconnect {u64 cap_id, u32 wanted, u32 issued, u64 snaprealm, u64 pathbase, u32 flock_len}, flock_len bytes of lock blob, v2 u64 snap_follows}; snaprealm_reconnect_t = ENCODE_START(1,1) {u64 ino, u64 seq, u64 parent}. v3: same caps map, raw 24-byte realm records until the end of the buffer; v2: u32 n + (ino, old cap record without header), realms raw; v1: map<ino, old_cap_reconnect_t> with the pre-FLOCK record. A session's reconnect completes only with a message without more. The kernel sends v3 (v2 when the previous connection lacked MDSENC and the MDS lacked bit 12) and switches to v5 multi-message only when the state exceeds INT_MAX - PAGE_SIZE; libcephfs sends v5 to an MDS with bit 12 and splits at about INT_MAX/2.
gates: CEPHFS_FEATURE_MULTI_RECONNECT (12) in the MDS bitmap: Linux v5.1+, Ceph 14.2.0+
features.notes: Generations (kclient expectations 7.1.2): kernels before v4.8 send v2 (v1 towards an MDS without FLOCK); v4.8 and later send v3; no kernel sends v4; every kernel v4.8-7.3 normally sends one v3 message. The kernel chooses the version from the previous daemon's OPEN bits and the previous connection's features. Ceph 13.x and older send one v3 message; 14.2.0+ send v5. Derived from code: since 14.1.0 the libcephfs single-message encoder writes realm records only in the v1 branch, so its v2/v3 reconnects carry no realms. Without bit 12 a kernel reconnect larger than RECONNECT_MAX_SIZE fails locally with -ENOSPC.

legacy_parts.note: Decoding MClientReconnect v1 (old_cap_reconnect_t map) and v2 (count plus old cap records); client paths towards an MDS without bit 12 (kernel v2 selection and -ENOSPC above RECONNECT_MAX_SIZE, libcephfs single-message v1-v3 without realms). Baseline clients send v3 (the 7.3 kernel, one message unless the state exceeds INT_MAX - PAGE_SIZE, then v5 parts) and v5 (libcephfs towards an MDS with bit 12), so v3 and v5 decoding are current. v1 and v2 come only from kernels before v4.8 and from clients talking to an MDS that lacks bit 12 and MDSENC or FLOCK. The kernel's -ENOSPC limit and the libcephfs single-message encoder apply only towards an MDS without bit 12, which the baseline MDS advertises.

features.group: MDS failover reconnect and NFS-Ganesha reclaim
features.name: Reconnect processing and outcomes
features.summary: How the MDS answers each reconnect: OPEN on success, CLOSE when it denies, REJECT when there is no session.
features.description: Server::handle_client_reconnect: no session gives REJECT "sessionless"; refuse_client_session gives CLOSE with error_string; a session that is not open gets CLOSE; a reconnect that arrives while the rank wants up:reconnect but is not yet in it (MDSMap delivery race) waits until the rank is in up:reconnect; mds_deny_all_reconnect, a rank no longer in (or wanting) reconnect, timeout evictions in progress (reconnect_evicting), a read-only MDS or missing required_client_features (after inferring features from version metadata for old clients) give CLOSE (denied) with the cluster-log line "denied reconnect attempt ...". On the last part (no `more` flag) the MDS registers the session with metrics and dmClock and sends OPEN (supported features and metric spec for Mimic+ clients, cap_auths). The per-cap and per-realm processing of accepted messages is F-CLU-082. A denied client that was open stays in the reconnect gather and is evicted (blocklisted by default) when the window times out. On OPEN the kernel calls it "reconnect success"; on CLOSE it drops all caps and dirty state (-EIO on mappings) and its unsafe requests, and restarts requests on a new session; libcephfs closes the session itself if it sees the rank past up:reconnect without having seen up:reconnect.
features.notes: Cap reconciliation in rejoin is owned by 01-cluster-membership-and-ha (resolve-and-rejoin page). The kernel clears dir-op cap bits from directory caps before reconnecting, so reconnect cannot seed Fc/Fr (kclient expectations 8). See also F-CLU-080 (reconnect window), F-CAPS-034 (cap side).

legacy_parts.note: infer_supported_features at reconnect; reconnect OPEN encoded as v1 for sessions without bit 8. Reconnect admission and outcomes are current for baseline sessions. Inferring features from ceph_version or kernel_version before the required-features test runs only for sessions stored without a bitmap (kernels up to v4.18, Ceph up to 13.2.1). The reconnect OPEN without supported_features and metric_spec goes only to sessions without bit 8.

features.group: MDS failover reconnect and NFS-Ganesha reclaim
features.name: Snap realm reconnect
features.summary: Clients report the snap realms they know in the reconnect message, and the MDS catches up clients whose realm sequence is old.
features.description: Realm records carry {ino, seq, parent}. The kernel sends every snap realm it knows; libcephfs sends only the realms of inodes that hold a cap from this rank (and, derived from code, none in its single-message v2/v3 reconnects). The MDS skips realms whose inode is being purged and records the others with add_reconnected_snaprealm; a client whose realm seq is older gets an MClientSnap UPDATE in MDCache::finish_snaprealm_reconnect.
features.notes: Snap realm semantics are owned by 08-snapshots-quotas-subvolumes. See also F-SNAP-032 (reconciliation at reconnect and rejoin).

features.group: MDS failover reconnect and NFS-Ganesha reclaim
features.name: Client reactions to MDSMap rank changes
features.summary: What clients do when a rank's state, address or presence changes in the MDSMap, which defines when they talk to a rank.
features.description: Kernel check_new_map: a rank beyond the new possible max is force-closed (unsafe requests dropped, caps removed, requests kicked); an address change closes the connection and sets RESTARTING; RESTARTING with state up:reconnect or later triggers the reconnect; a transition from below up:active to up:active or later kicks new requests and in-flight flushes and resets max_size requests; a laggy rank makes the kernel open sessions to its export targets. New requests go only to ranks in up:active or later (up:clientreplay is not enough), renewals from up:reconnect on, metrics only to up:active. MDSMap entries with state <= 0 (creating, starting, standby-replay) are invisible to the kernel. libcephfs handle_mds_map marks the connection down for a down rank, sends reconnect at exactly up:reconnect, closes the session on a missed reconnect, kicks at active or stopping, and sends requests to active or stopping ranks.
features.notes: The MDS influences these reactions only through what its beacons put in the MDSMap (owned by 01-cluster-membership-and-ha). The kernel MDSMap decoder and its quirks are in kclient expectations 3.3. See also F-CLU-006 (kernel MDSMap decode).

features.group: MDS failover reconnect and NFS-Ganesha reclaim
features.name: Session reclaim (MClientReclaim with CEPH_RECLAIM_RESET)
features.summary: A restarted NFS-Ganesha (new libcephfs instance, new global id) destroys the MDS session of its previous incarnation, identified by a uuid, so the dead instance's caps and locks are released immediately.
features.description: MClientReclaim = string uuid, u32 flags (CEPH_RECLAIM_RESET = 1, FLAG_FINISH = 1<<31); MClientReclaimReply = i32 result (raw host errno), u32 epoch (OSDMap epoch after the eviction), entity_addrvec_t addrs (old session address). The MDS ignores a reclaim without session, drops it without MAY_READ fs caps, waits for up:clientreplay, drops it if the requesting session is not open or stale, answers -EINVAL for an empty uuid or flags other than exactly RESET (FLAG_FINISH combined with another flag gives -EINVAL). A session whose metadata uuid matches is checked for the same cephx auth_name as the requester (-EPERM otherwise); it is killed (if already blocklisted or mds_session_blocklist_on_evict is false) or evicted with blocklisting, and the reply is sent when that completes. No match gives result 0, no address, epoch 0. libcephfs ceph_start_reclaim opens a session (metadata timeout only, no root) to every rank 0..num_in-1 in turn, requires RECLAIM_CLIENT in that rank's OPEN (-EOPNOTSUPP), sends one reclaim per rank and returns -ENOENT if no rank returned addresses; after a RESET reclaim ceph_finish_reclaim sends nothing; ceph_set_uuid then closes all sessions so that the mount reopens them with the uuid. A second session opening with a uuid still owned by a live session is rejected. auth_name is journaled in ESession so a session recreated by replay can still be reclaimed.
gates: MDS bit CEPHFS_FEATURE_RECLAIM_CLIENT (10), Ceph 14.2.0+; no kernel advertises it
features.notes: FSAL_CEPH (nfs-ganesha V15.7) runs ceph_set_session_timeout(300), ceph_start_reclaim(uuid, RESET), ceph_finish_reclaim, ceph_set_uuid at every cmount creation (daemon start and every new export key) and reclaims on rados_cluster nodeid takeover; the uuid is ganesha-0x<CityHash64(nodeid, user, fs, cmount path)>. Code observation: libcephfs reclaim results are sticky per client, so a later reclaim for an unknown uuid returns 0 instead of -ENOENT once one matched (libcephfs-fuse-ganesha 8). The non-RESET path is unreachable because the MDS rejects other flags. See also F-CLU-096 (clientreplay held for pending reclaims).

legacy_parts.note: Non-RESET reclaim handling: the ceph_assert(0) branch of Server::reclaim_session, the FLAG_FINISH path of Server::handle_client_reclaim and the reclaiming_from pairing it would complete. NFS-Ganesha V15.7 always calls ceph_start_reclaim with CEPH_RECLAIM_RESET, and that path is current. The MDS answers -EINVAL to any flags other than exactly RESET, so the non-RESET branch of Server::reclaim_session (ceph_assert(0)) cannot run. libcephfs sends FLAG_FINISH only after a successful non-RESET reclaim, so baseline clients never send it, and because the RESET path clears reclaiming_from at once the FLAG_FINISH handler would find no pending reclaim.

features.name: MClientRequest versioned head (head v1, v2, v3)
features.summary: The fixed request head every metadata request starts with, in the three versioned forms current clients send.
features.description: MClientRequest is message v6/compat 1; for message version 4 and above the head is the versioned ceph_mds_request_head: u16 version, u64 oldest_client_tid, u32 mdsmap_epoch (ignored by the MDS), u32 flags, u8 num_retry, u8 num_fwd, u16 num_releases, u32 op, u32 caller_uid, u32 caller_gid, u64 ino, 56-byte args union (v1, 98 bytes); u32 ext_num_retry, u32 ext_num_fwd (v2, 106 bytes); u32 struct_len, u32 owner_uid, u32 owner_gid (v3, 118 bytes). The decoder skips unknown trailing head bytes by struct_len and throws if it consumed more; for v1/v2 heads it sets owner = caller. Clients send head v1 if the MDS lacks 32BITS_RETRY_FWD, v2 if it lacks HAS_OWNER_UIDGID, else v3; owner_uid/gid carry the (idmapped) fsuid/fsgid for CREATE, MKNOD, MKDIR and SYMLINK and -1 otherwise; caller_uid/gid are used for MDS cap checks. The kernel uses message version 4 for head v1 and 6 for head v2/v3.
gates: MDS bit CEPHFS_FEATURE_32BITS_RETRY_FWD (18) selects head v2+
MDS bit CEPHFS_FEATURE_HAS_OWNER_UIDGID (20) selects head v3
features.notes: Generations (kclient expectations 7.1.2): head v1 from kernels v5.11-v6.5 (and later kernels towards an MDS without bit 18), v2 from v6.6, v3 from v6.7; Ceph v1 up to 16.2.13 and 17.2.6, v2 in 16.2.14-16.2.15, 17.2.7, 18.1.0-18.2.0, v3 from 17.2.8, 18.2.1, 19.2.0. On an idmapped mount a kernel session without bit 20 fails CREATE/MKNOD/MKDIR/SYMLINK with -EIO unless enable_unsafe_idmap is set. For new-inode ops an owner uid (or gid when the parent is not setgid) of -1 trips ceph_assert in Server::prepare_new_inode, whatever the head version.

legacy_parts.note: Decoding head v1 and v2 (ext counters from the 8-bit fields, owner_uid/gid set to caller_uid/gid); the kernel's message v4 labelling for head v1. Towards an MDS with bits 18 and 20 the 7.3 kernel sends message v6 with head v3 and libcephfs at this commit sends head v3, so head v3 decoding is current. Head v1 comes from kernels v5.11-v6.5, CentOS Stream 8 and Ceph up to 16.2.13 and 17.2.6, and head v2 from Linux v6.6 and Ceph 16.2.14-16.2.15, 17.2.7 and 18.1.0-18.2.0. Current clients choose head v1 or v2 only towards an MDS without bit 18 or 20.

features.name: Legacy 88-byte request head (message version below 4)
features.summary: Fallback request head without a version field, used by old clients and by any client talking to an MDS without FS_BTIME.
features.description: For MClientRequest message versions below 4 the head is the raw 88-byte ceph_mds_request_head_legacy (no version field, 48-byte args). The MDS decoder synthesizes version 0, widens the 8-bit num_retry/num_fwd into the 32-bit fields, sets owner_uid/gid = caller_uid/gid and strips CEPH_SETATTR_BTIME from a setattr mask. Current clients fall back to it only when the MDS connection lacks FS_BTIME (bit 59).
gates: connection feature FS_BTIME (59) on the MDS connection
features.notes: Users: every kernel up to v5.10 (message v2), Ceph 10.2.x and older (message v3); later clients only towards an MDS without FS_BTIME. Candidate floor F4 (bit 16 or 17) leaves it unused (kclient expectations 7.1.7).

legacy.note: Message versions below 4 come from kernels up to v5.10 (message v2) and Ceph 10.2.x and older (message v3). Later kernels and libcephfs use the legacy head only towards an MDS connection without FS_BTIME (bit 59), which the baseline MDS advertises. The 7.3 kernel and libcephfs at this commit send message v6 with head v3.

features.name: Request message tail: stamp, gid_list, alternate_name, fscrypt fields
features.summary: Fields that follow the paths and release records of a request, added over message versions 2 to 6.
features.description: After head, path, path2 and the release records come: v2 utime stamp (the client's operation time, which becomes ctime/mtime/atime/btime of the mutation; MDS time if zero); v4 vector<u64> gid_list (supplementary groups for MDS cap checks); v5 string alternate_name (fscrypt ciphertext of long names, or the original spelling of a charmap name; longer than mds_alternate_name_max, 8 KiB, gives -ENAMETOOLONG; returned in LeaseStat v2); v6 vector<u8> fscrypt_auth and vector<u8> fscrypt_file. Trailing bytes are ignored. The kernel writes the complete v6 tail even in messages it labels v3 or v4, and the MDS reads only what the header version covers, so with message version 4 alternate_name and the fscrypt fields are ignored and with version 3 also gid_list.
features.notes: Generations: kernels up to v5.10 send message v2 without gid_list, so they never send supplementary groups; v5.11-v6.5 send v3/v4; v6.6+ the full v6 tail. Ceph sends v3 (10.2.x), v4 (11.x-15.x), v5 (16.x-17.x), v6 (18.x+) (kclient expectations 7.1.2). fscrypt semantics (fscrypt_file size rules, last-block truncate) are owned by 04-namespace-and-posix-operations.

legacy_parts.note: Decoding request messages v2-v5 (tail cut after stamp, gid_list or alternate_name), including v3/v4-labelled kernel messages whose extra tail fields the MDS ignores. The 7.3 kernel and libcephfs at this commit send MClientRequest v6 to an MDS with bits 18 and 20, so the full tail (stamp, gid_list, alternate_name, fscrypt_auth, fscrypt_file) is current. Message versions 2-5 come from kernels up to v6.5 (v2 up to v5.10, v3/v4 from v5.11, also CentOS Stream 8) and Ceph clients up to 17.x, or from current kernels towards an MDS without bit 18.

features.name: Request flags REPLAY, WANT_DENTRY and ASYNC
features.summary: Three head flags that change how the MDS treats a request.
features.description: CEPH_MDS_FLAG_REPLAY (1) is set on a resend of a request that already got an unsafe reply: no early reply, embedded releases ignored, a completed-request hit gives a traceless safe reply, queued for clientreplay in up:reconnect, and the stray-directory space check skipped. CEPH_MDS_FLAG_WANT_DENTRY (2) (kernel whenever r_parent is set; libcephfs when the request has a dentry and always for LOOKUP/LOOKUPSNAP) makes the reply include the dentry trace, including the null dentry on -ENOENT, and turns a completed CREATE retry into LOOKUP instead of GETATTR. CEPH_MDS_FLAG_ASYNC (4) marks kernel async create/unlink; in up:reconnect it is queued like a replay, otherwise processed normally.
features.notes: The kernel sets ASYNC only when the directory cap has Fx|Dc or Fx|Dr, which the C++ MDS at this commit never grants, so no async request reaches it (leases-lock-caches-and-async-dirops 8, G1). libcephfs never sets ASYNC.

features.name: Request argument union per op
features.summary: The 56-byte args union in the request head and which ops use which member.
features.description: Members (offset:size): getattr {mask} for GETATTR, LOOKUP, LOOKUPSNAP; setattr {mode, uid, gid, mtime, atime, size, old_size, mask (CEPH_SETATTR_* bits 0-14), btime} for SETATTR (uid/gid are also passed to every MDS cap check as the new owner); readdir {frag, max_entries (0 = no limit), max_bytes (0 = 512 KiB + max xattr size), flags, offset_hash} for READDIR and LSSNAP; mknod {mode, rdev}; mkdir {mode}; open {flags (CEPH_O_*), mode, stripe_unit, stripe_count, object_size, pool (only with CREATEPOOLID), mask, old_size} for OPEN and CREATE; setxattr {flags (CREATE/REPLACE/REMOVE/REMOVE2), osdmap_epoch}; setlayout {raw 28-byte ceph_file_layout}; filelock_change {rule, type, owner, pid, start, length, wait} for SETFILELOCK/GETFILELOCK; lookupino {mask, snapid, parent, hash}; snapdiff {frag, max_entries, max_bytes, flags, offset_hash, snap_other, mask}; blockdiff {scan_idx, max_objects}.
features.notes: Open flags are translated to CEPH_O_* (RDONLY 0, WRONLY 1, RDWR 2, CREAT 0100, EXCL 0200, TRUNC 01000, DIRECTORY 0200000, NOFOLLOW 0400000); O_APPEND, O_SYNC, O_DSYNC, O_DIRECT never reach the MDS. Server::check_access reads args.setattr.uid/gid for every op, i.e. unrelated union bytes for non-setattr ops (wire-protocol 8). Op semantics are owned by 04-namespace-and-posix-operations.

features.name: Embedded cap and dentry-lease release records
features.summary: Clients piggy-back cap and dentry-lease releases on a request so the MDS does not have to revoke them first.
features.description: head.num_releases records follow the two paths: raw ceph_mds_request_release (ino, cap_id, caps, wanted, seq, issue_seq, mseq, dname_seq, dname_len; 44 bytes) followed by dname_len name bytes without a length prefix. A record with a name releases the dentry lease on (ino = parent dir, dname) and then the cap on ino. The MDS processes them with Locker::process_request_cap_release before dispatch, only for non-replay client requests; records with a stale mseq or another cap_id are ignored, and they are cleared for retried requests arriving in up:reconnect. The kernel drops the released bits locally before sending; libcephfs always emits a record for the parent directory's cap on a dentry release. Both clients strip the records on replays and on resends during reconnect.
features.notes: Cap and lease semantics are owned by 03-caps-leases-and-locking. See also F-CAPS-029 (MDS processing).

features.name: Request data segment per op
features.summary: Ops that carry a blob in the message data segment, and its format.
features.description: CREATE, MKNOD, MKDIR and SYMLINK: optional initial xattrs, u32 count + (string key, u32 len + value) (the kernel sends system.posix_acl_access/default from ceph_pre_init_acls and the LSM security label; libcephfs ACL blobs), decoded by Server::prepare_new_inode as the new inode's xattr map without a try block. SETXATTR: the xattr value (for ceph.* vxattrs the textual value). SETATTR with CEPH_SETATTR_SIZE on an fscrypt file: ENCODE_START(1) {u64 change_attr, u64 file_offset, u64 block_size} followed by the last block, at most mds_fscrypt_last_block_max_size (4 KiB) plus header (-EINVAL if larger); a change_attr that differs from the inode gives -EAGAIN. MKSNAP: SnapPayload ENCODE_START(1,1) {map<string,string> metadata}, undecodable payload ignored. SNAP_METADATA: string key, string value, u32 op_flag; undecodable gives -EBADMSG.
features.notes: The kernel retries an fscrypt truncate up to 20 times on -EAGAIN; libcephfs does not retry and the error reaches the application (libcephfs-fuse-ganesha 8).

features.name: Path encoding on the wire
features.summary: How clients name the object of a request: an inode number plus a relative path, with snapshot directories encoded as empty components.
features.description: filepath = u8 1, u64 ino, string path (ino 0 = relative). The kernel sends (ino, "") for a head inode, (parent ino, name) for a dentry op with the parent locked, and otherwise a path relative to the nearest ancestor whose inode is a head inode, where each .snap directory is an empty component (a/.snap/s1/b is (ino(a), "/s1/b"), LSSNAP of a/.snap is (ino(a), "")); the snapshot id itself is never on the wire; mount uses (1, server path without leading "/"). libcephfs uses #ino or #parent_ino/name and builds snapped paths from the nearest non-snap ancestor. The MDS keeps empty components of wire-decoded paths, interprets an empty first component as the snapdir and rejects empty components elsewhere with -EINVAL. libcephfs sends requests relative to any inode number it has cached.
features.notes: If the parent was not locked and r_parent no longer matches the ino in the built path, the kernel switches r_parent to that inode with a one-time WARN. Path traversal is owned by 05-metadata-cache-and-dirfrags.

features.name: Op code numbering and the write bit
features.summary: The CEPH_MDS_OP_* numbers, the 0x1000 write bit and its effects, and which ops each client sends.
features.description: Client ops: LOOKUP 0x100, GETATTR 0x101, LOOKUPHASH 0x102, LOOKUPPARENT 0x103, LOOKUPINO 0x104, LOOKUPNAME 0x105, GETVXATTR 0x106, SETXATTR 0x1105, RMXATTR 0x1106, SETLAYOUT 0x1107, SETATTR 0x1108, SETFILELOCK 0x1109, GETFILELOCK 0x110, SETDIRLAYOUT 0x110a, MKNOD 0x1201, LINK 0x1202, UNLINK 0x1203, RENAME 0x1204, MKDIR 0x1220, RMDIR 0x1221, SYMLINK 0x1222, CREATE 0x1301, OPEN 0x302, READDIR 0x305, LOOKUPSNAP 0x400, MKSNAP 0x1400, RMSNAP 0x1401, LSSNAP 0x402, RENAMESNAP 0x1403, READDIR_SNAPDIFF 0x1404, FILE_BLOCKDIFF 0x1405, SNAP_METADATA 0x1406; 0x15xx are internal ops (from a client: -EOPNOTSUPP, or -EROFS first) and DUMMY 0x107 gives -EOPNOTSUPP. may_write() is the write bit or OPEN with O_CREAT|O_TRUNC; it decides -EROFS on a read-only cache and whether a success is recorded as a completed request (never for SETFILELOCK). IS_CEPH_MDS_OP_NEWINODE = CREATE, MKNOD, MKDIR, SYMLINK (the ops that consume head.ino and owner_uid/gid).
features.notes: READDIR_SNAPDIFF and FILE_BLOCKDIFF are read-like ops with the write bit, so they fail with -EROFS on a read-only cache and are recorded as completed. may_write tests args.open.flags against host O_CREAT|O_TRUNC while handlers use CEPH_O_*; the values only match on hosts with the asm-generic Linux values (wire-protocol 8). The kernel never sends LOOKUPHASH, READDIR_SNAPDIFF, FILE_BLOCKDIFF or SNAP_METADATA; libcephfs never sends SETLAYOUT or SETDIRLAYOUT. Handlers are owned by 04-namespace-and-posix-operations. See also F-NS-001 (dispatch to handlers).

features.name: Client-chosen inode number (head.ino)
features.summary: Create-type requests can name the inode number to use (head.ino).
features.description: See F-NS-041. Wire and client side: head.ino is the ino field of the request head (F-PROTO-065); IS_CEPH_MDS_OP_NEWINODE ops (CREATE, MKNOD, MKDIR, SYMLINK) consume it. Clients set it to the target ino of an earlier unsafe reply when they replay a request, and the kernel sets it to a delegated ino for an async create and expects the MDS to create exactly that ino. In up:reconnect the MDS reserves a carried ino with add_replay_ino_alloc. A number that is neither in the session preallocation nor free in the rank InoTable is not replaced but trips an assert (strict interval_set erase); only a number found in replay_taken_inos is replaced, with the cluster-log error "specified ino X but mds allocated Y", which the client does not see.
features.notes: Against the C++ MDS at this commit the kernel never issues async creates (Dc, the Fc bit on a directory cap, is never granted; F-CAPS-054), so head.ino is only used by replays. Delegated inode numbers are owned by 03-caps-leases-and-locking.

features.name: Client-side rank selection and the hints the MDS provides
features.summary: Clients choose the rank for each request themselves, from caps, fragtree delegation hints in DirStat and random choice; any rank can receive any request.
features.description: The kernel (__choose_mds) uses a forward target first, then the inode or the dentry (parent dir plus name hash with the directory's dl_dir_hash), a dirfrag delegation from the fragtree (a random replica from dist for read-only requests, else the frag auth), then the auth-cap rank (or any cap rank) and finally a random up rank; it sends only to ranks in up:active or later. libcephfs (choose_target_mds) does the same with auth_is_best true for write-bit ops, OPEN, READDIR and some GETATTR masks, and sends LOOKUPINO, LOOKUPPARENT, LOOKUPNAME and LOOKUPHASH to rand() % num_in. The MDS supplies DirStat.auth (-1 = same as the dir inode's auth) and DirStat.dist (replica ranks plus self when the dir is auth and replicated and mds_forward_all_requests_to_auth is false), the dirfragtree in InodeStat and dir_layout.dl_dir_hash (mds_default_dir_hash, default 2 = rjenkins, on new directories).
features.notes: The kernel hashes names with the VFS d_name.hash for dl_dir_hash 0 or 1 and with rjenkins for 2 (other values yield 0xffffffff); readdir offsets always use ceph_str_hash(dl_dir_hash, name) (kclient expectations 3.6.1). Subtree authority is owned by 07-multi-mds. See also F-CACHE-079 (DirStat hints), F-MULTI-050 (hot-directory replication).

features.name: Request forwarding (MClientRequestForward)
features.summary: A rank that is not authoritative tells the client to resend the request to another rank; it never relays the request itself.
features.description: MDCache::request_forward calls MDSRank::forward_message_mds, which sends MClientRequestForward(tid, dest_mds, num_fwd = request num_fwd + 1, client_must_resend = true) and cleans up the request; payload i32 dest_mds, i32 num_fwd, bool client_must_resend. Every member of a batched getattr/lookup is forwarded; an internal op gets -EXDEV and a request from an MDS is dropped. The kernel reads next_mds and fwd_seq (ignoring client_must_resend): if fwd_seq <= its stored count or >= U32_MAX it aborts the request with -EMULTIHOP, otherwise it resets r_attempts, stores the count and resends to next_mds; libcephfs does the same. The resent request carries the count in ext_num_fwd/num_fwd. MDCache::path_traverse discovers (replicates) instead of forwarding again when the path depth is below the request's num_fwd, which bounds forward ping-pong between ranks.
features.notes: A forward for a request that already applied an (unsafe) reply or recorded an error hits BUG_ON in the kernel handle_forward ("forward race not possible; mds would drop") (kclient expectations 8). Before v5.19 (and in CentOS Stream 8) kernels ignore a forward whose 8-bit count wrapped, so the request is not resent (derived from code). Forwarding policy is owned by 07-multi-mds. See also F-CACHE-044 (forward or discover), F-NS-053 (which rank serves each op), F-MULTI-018 (migration).

features.name: Retry counters and attempt limits (32BITS_RETRY_FWD)
features.summary: Each resend of a request carries an attempt count; 8-bit counters limit old clients to 256 attempts or forwards.
features.description: Every send increments the client attempt counter; the head carries attempts - 1 in ext_num_retry and its low 8 bits in num_retry. Both clients reset the counter after a forward, and the kernel also after a local session teardown. Without the MDS bit 18 clients use head v1 (8-bit counters only) and abort the request with -EMULTIHOP after 256 attempts; with it at U32_MAX. The MDS uses a non-zero retry count only to consult the completed-request table and, in up:reconnect, to queue a completed request for clientreplay and drop its embedded releases; forward counts are always widened to 32 bits on decode.
gates: MDS bit CEPHFS_FEATURE_32BITS_RETRY_FWD (18): Linux v6.6+, Ceph 16.2.14, 17.2.7, 18.2.0+
features.notes: Kernels v5.19-v6.5 abort at 256 retries or forwards; before v5.19 nothing stops the wrap (kclient expectations 7.1.2). Completed-request handling is owned by 04-namespace-and-posix-operations.

legacy_parts.note: Widening of 8-bit num_retry/num_fwd from legacy and v1 heads; the clients' 256-attempt limit towards an MDS without bit 18. The baseline MDS advertises bit 18, so the 7.3 kernel and libcephfs send 32-bit counters (head v3) and abort only at U32_MAX. The 8-bit counters and the 256-attempt abort apply to clients without bit 18 (kernels before v6.6, CentOS Stream 8, Ceph before 16.2.14, 17.2.7 and 18.1.0) and to current clients only towards an MDS without bit 18.

features.name: Request identity, tid ordering and requests without a session
features.summary: Requests are identified by (client, tid); the MDS drops duplicates of an active request and requests from clients without an open session.
features.description: tids increase per client incarnation, but libcephfs assigns the tid when a call enters make_request and the request may then wait for an MDSMap or a session open, or be forwarded, so requests of one session can reach a rank out of tid order. MDCache::request_start drops a request whose metareqid_t(client, tid) is already active. Requests from a client without a session, or with a closed, closing or killing session, are dropped without reply. oldest_client_tid is the lowest outstanding tid that is not SETFILELOCK, so it lags behind the slowest outstanding request.

features.name: MClientReply head and error codes
features.summary: Every request is answered with MClientReply: a 15-byte head, the trace, an op-specific extra blob and a snap trace.
features.description: Front payload: raw ceph_mds_reply_head {u32 op (copied from the request), u32 result (errorcode32_t: 0 or a negative Linux errno), u32 mdsmap_epoch (0 in early replies, set only on the final reply), u8 safe, u8 is_dentry, u8 is_target}, then bufferlist trace_bl, bufferlist extra_bl, bufferlist snapbl; message version 1; header.tid = request tid. The kernel dispatches the extra parser on the head op, requires the trace and the whole front to be consumed exactly, and matches replies by tid on the session the request was last sent to (others are dropped); libcephfs asserts that the front is consumed. Result codes produced: -EINVAL, -ENOENT, -EPERM, -EACCES, -ENOTDIR, -EISDIR, -EROFS, -ENOTEMPTY, -ESTALE, -ENAMETOOLONG, -ENOSPC, -EEXIST, -EAGAIN, -ENODATA, -EBUSY, -EXDEV, -EOPNOTSUPP, -EDOM, -ENXIO, -EMLINK, -EIO, -EINTR, -EINPROGRESS, -EDEADLK, -EBADMSG; the MDS never returns -EDQUOT (quota is enforced by clients).
features.notes: -EMULTIHOP and -EJUKEBOX are generated client side only. POSIX permission bits are not checked by the MDS except through uid/gid-restricted MDS cap grants (wire-protocol 3.9.7).

features.name: Reply trace layout
features.summary: The trace tells the client which directory, dentry and inode the request touched, so it can update its cache without another round trip.
features.description: trace_bl = [InodeStat(dir inode), DirStat(dir frag), string dname, LeaseStat(dentry)] if is_dentry, then [InodeStat(target)] if is_target; nothing else. snapbl is the snap trace of the target's realm (or the dir's realm without target), empty for snapshot ids; clients apply it before the trace. Error replies can carry a trace (-ENOENT with WANT_DENTRY gives a null-dentry trace). No trace is built for a reply that follows an early reply or for a re-executed REPLAY request. The dir InodeStat is encoded without a realm and may issue caps on the parent. Traceless replies also occur for completed requests and with mds_inject_traceless_reply_probability (default 0, test only); clients then look the target up themselves (the kernel follow-up LOOKUP for creates, libcephfs verify_reply_trace).
features.notes: libcephfs asserts that the trace of a safe reply following an unsafe one is empty, and a traceless reply to a request whose dentry is no longer linked hits ceph_abort_msg in verify_reply_trace (libcephfs-fuse-ganesha 7.1).

features.name: InodeStat versioned encoding (v9, REPLY_ENCODING)
features.summary: The per-inode record in traces and readdir listings, in the versioned form sent to clients that advertise bit 9.
features.description: ENCODE_START(9, 1) { u64 ino, u64 snapid, u32 rdev, u64 version (2 x version + 1 if projected), u64 xattr_version, raw 33-byte reply cap {caps, wanted, cap_id, seq, mseq, realm, flags (CEPH_CAP_FLAG_AUTH)}, raw 28-byte legacy layout, ctime, mtime, atime, u32 time_warp_seq, size, max_size, truncate_size, u32 truncate_seq, mode, uid, gid, nlink, nfiles, nsubdirs, rbytes, rfiles, rsubdirs, rctime, dirfragtree, symlink, 8-byte dir_layout, xattr blob, inline_version, inline_data, quota ENCODE_START(1,1){max_bytes, max_files}, pool_ns, btime, change_attr; v2 dir_pin; v3 snap_btime; v4 rsnaps; v5 snap_metadata; v6 fscrypt flag; v7 fscrypt_auth, fscrypt_file; v8 optmetadata (kind 1 CHARMAP, kind 2 QUARANTINE); v9 subvolume_id }. The fixed prefix up to the fragtree count is byte-identical to the kernel's 221-byte struct ceph_mds_reply_inode. The kernel requires compat 1, skips snap_metadata, the fscrypt flag and optmetadata, and uses struct_len to skip later fields.
gates: client bit CEPHFS_FEATURE_REPLY_ENCODING (9): Linux v5.1+, Ceph 14.2.0+
features.notes: Code observations (wire-protocol 8): optmetadata_singleton::get_kind treats only kinds > 3 as unknown, so kind 3 indexes past the variant table; for a quarantined inode the encoder emits a default record (enabled, timestamp 0) instead of the stored one; for snapped inodes cap_id and wanted are left uninitialised. Ceph 19.2.3 and 20.2.x send v8; this tree and 21.x send v9. Field semantics are owned by 05-metadata-cache-and-dirfrags.

features.name: Legacy (connection-feature-conditional) reply encodings
features.summary: Fallback InodeStat, DirStat and LeaseStat encodings without ENCODE_START headers, for clients that do not advertise bit 9.
features.description: Without REPLY_ENCODING the InodeStat has no header: the same fields up to symlink, then dir_layout only with DIRLAYOUTHASH, xattrs always, inline_version + inline_data with MDS_INLINE_DATA, quota with MDS_QUOTA, pool_ns with FS_FILE_LAYOUT_V2, btime + change_attr with FS_BTIME, and nothing from struct v2 on. DirStat is the same fields without header; LeaseStat is u16 mask, u32 duration_ms, u32 seq (10 bytes, no alternate_name). The kernel legacy decoder takes field presence from the MDS's advertised connection features while the MDS uses the negotiated intersection; the two agree only because each kernel advertises every feature whose field it decodes.
features.notes: Users: kernels up to v5.0, Ceph up to 13.2.x, and every session with inferred features. Candidate floor F2 (bit 12 or 9) leaves it unused (kclient expectations 7.1.7).

legacy.note: The header-less InodeStat, DirStat and LeaseStat go only to sessions without bit 9: kernels up to v5.0, Ceph clients up to 13.2.x and sessions whose bits were inferred. The 7.3 kernel and libcephfs at this commit advertise bit 9 and receive InodeStat v9, DirStat v1 and LeaseStat v2.

features.name: DirStat and LeaseStat records
features.summary: The directory-fragment record and the dentry-lease record inside traces and readdir entries.
features.description: DirStat = ENCODE_START(1,1) {u32 frag, i32 auth, set<i32> dist} from CDir::encode_dirstat. LeaseStat = ENCODE_START(2,1) {u16 mask, u32 duration_ms, u32 seq, v2 string alternate_name} from Locker::encode_lease. A real dentry lease (Locker::issue_client_lease) has mask CEPH_LEASE_VALID plus CEPH_LEASE_PRIMARY_LINK for a primary dentry, duration 30000 ms (client_lease_durations[1]) and seq = ++lease seq; when the client cannot get a lease (snapshot, dentry lock not leaseable, stray dir, dir filelock leaseable by the client, or the client holds Fs/Fx on the dir) a null lease is sent (mask 0, duration 0, seq 0) that still carries alternate_name.
features.notes: Lease semantics (validity, revocation, PRIMARY_LINK and async unlink) are owned by 03-caps-leases-and-locking. Without CEPHFS_FEATURE_REPLY_ENCODING the lease record is the raw 10-byte ceph_mds_reply_lease {u16 mask, u32 duration_ms, u32 seq} (F-PROTO-082). In a trace the order is [dir InodeStat][DirStat][dname][lease][target InodeStat]; readdir entries are [dname][lease][InodeStat]. The kernel rejects struct_compat != 1, reads alternate_name only for struct_v >= 2 and skips to struct_len; both client families use alternate_name. See also F-CAPS-038 (lease issue), F-CACHE-079 (DirStat hints).

legacy_parts.note: Header-less DirStat and raw 10-byte ceph_mds_reply_lease for sessions without CEPHFS_FEATURE_REPLY_ENCODING. Baseline clients advertise bit 9 and receive DirStat v1 and LeaseStat v2 with alternate_name. The header-less DirStat and the raw 10-byte LeaseStat go only to sessions without bit 9 (kernels up to v5.0, Ceph up to 13.2.x, sessions with inferred features).

features.name: Caps, xattrs and inline data carried inside InodeStat
features.summary: Wire view of the caps, xattr blob and inline data that an InodeStat can carry.
features.description: See F-CAPS-009 (cap issued with a reply), F-NS-068 (xattr blob inclusion rules) and F-CAPS-015 (inline data and xattrs versioned per client). Wire-specific: inline_version is CEPH_INLINE_NONE when the inode is not inline and 0 when the data is not sent; xattr_version is 0 when the blob is dropped; max_size is the client's writeable range. During readdir an estimate is checked against max_bytes and -ENOSPC stops the listing.
features.notes: libcephfs asserts that inline_version becomes > 0 after a GETATTR asking for inline data (libcephfs-fuse-ganesha 4).

legacy_parts.note: Inline data content in InodeStat (inline_version other than CEPH_INLINE_NONE, including 0 when the data is withheld). New inodes get inline_version CEPH_INLINE_NONE unless the MDSMap enables inline data, which only the deprecated `ceph fs set <fs> inline_data true --yes-i-really-really-mean-it` does. No mgr module, cephadm, Rook or tool sets it, so inline_version 0 (data withheld) and non-empty inline data occur only on file systems where that deprecated setting was used.

features.name: Snap trace encoding and format selection
features.summary: The snap realm chain sent with replies, cap imports and MClientSnap, in an old raw form or a versioned form chosen by client bit 19.
features.description: A snap trace is the concatenation of realm records from the target realm up to the root realm. Old element (SnapRealmInfo): raw 48-byte ceph_mds_snap_realm {ino, created, parent, parent_since, seq, u32 num_snaps, u32 num_prior_parent_snaps} followed by those u64 snap ids. New element (SnapRealmInfoNew): ENCODE_START(2,1) {old element, utime last_modified, u64 change_attr, v2 u32 flags (SNAPDIR_VISIBILITY = 4)}. Server::get_snap_trace picks the new form for sessions with NEW_SNAPREALM_INFO; libcephfs picks its decoder from the MDS's bit, so the two sides agree because the MDS always advertises it. A snap trace the kernel cannot parse makes it blocklist itself.
gates: client bit CEPHFS_FEATURE_NEW_SNAPREALM_INFO (19): never in Linux, Ceph 17.2.8 and 18.2.0+
features.notes: No kernel advertises bit 19, so every kernel needs the old format (kclient expectations 7.1.7). Snap realm semantics are owned by 08-snapshots-quotas-subvolumes. Element order is child first up to the root realm (parent 0) or the global realm; my_snaps and prior_parent_snaps are descending le64 lists; clients test only flag 4. Traces travel in MClientReply.snapbl (only for replies whose snapid is CEPH_NOSNAP; LSSNAP replies carry the directory realm's trace; replies about snapshots carry none), in MClientSnap and in MClientCaps IMPORT. See also F-SNAP-008 (contents and client interpretation), F-SNAP-006.

features.name: Readdir and LSSNAP reply format and ordering contract
features.summary: The extra_bl of directory listings and the ordering and size rules clients enforce on it.
features.description: READDIR and READDIR_SNAPDIFF extra_bl: DirStat, u32 num, u16 flags, then num x (string dname, LeaseStat, InodeStat). flags: FRAG_END (1) when the frag is exhausted, FRAG_COMPLETE (0x100) when it was also read from its start, HASH_ORDER (0x200) and OFFSET_HASH (0x400) when the request had CEPH_READDIR_REPLY_BITFLAGS. Entries come in dirfrag key order (24-bit name hash, name, snapid); resume is by path2 = last name, else by offset_hash; a non-existent frag is adjusted to the one containing offset_hash; the .ceph inode is skipped. LSSNAP: empty DirStat (frag 0, auth -1), entries named by snapshot (long name _<name>_<ino> for inherited snaps) with lease {VALID, 0xffffffff ms, seq 0} and the dir InodeStat at that snapid. The kernel sends max_entries from its preallocated buffer and fails a reply with more entries (-EIO), requires non-decreasing hash order from the continuation point (readdir -EIO otherwise), adopts the returned frag, and needs the extra on every successful READDIR/LSSNAP. libcephfs sends max_entries = max_bytes = 0, re-chooses the frag on -EAGAIN and parses the extra only when the trace has the target.
features.notes: Derived from code: a successful READDIR without extra makes the kernel dereference a NULL DirStat, and a reply whose head op is READDIR/LSSNAP with entries for a request without a readdir buffer hits BUG_ON (kclient expectations 8). Kernels before v4.7 do not send REPLY_BITFLAGS; the flags field then reads as the old u8 end, u8 complete pair. Readdir semantics are owned by 04-namespace-and-posix-operations. See also F-NS-032, F-NS-033.

legacy_parts.note: READDIR handling without CEPH_READDIR_REPLY_BITFLAGS: frag adjustment that ignores offset_hash and clears the resume name, and replies without HASH_ORDER/OFFSET_HASH whose flags such clients read as the old u8 end, u8 complete pair. The 7.3 kernel and libcephfs set CEPH_READDIR_REPLY_BITFLAGS on every READDIR and LSSNAP, and libcephfs also on READDIR_SNAPDIFF, so replies carry HASH_ORDER and OFFSET_HASH and offset_hash selects the frag. Requests without the flag come only from kernels before v4.7.
evidence_notes: linux-v4.7/fs/ceph/dir.c:409 (first fetched tag that sets the flag

features.name: CREATE reply: created inode and delegated inode ranges
features.summary: A CREATE that made a new inode reports its number in extra_bl, as openc_response_t (with delegated inode ranges) or as a raw u64.
features.description: Server::set_reply_extra_bl writes openc_response_t = ENCODE_START(1,1) {u64 created_ino, interval_set<inodeno_t> delegated_inos} when the MDS member mds_allow_async_dirops is true and the client has DELEG_INO; else a raw u64 ino when the connection has REPLY_CREATE_INODE; else nothing (an empty extra means "opened an existing file"). Both clients choose the parser from the MDS's DELEG_INO bit, not from the bytes. Delegation: when mds_client_delegate_inos_pct is non-zero, the request is not a queued replay and the session holds fewer than 250 delegated inodes (defaults), the set is topped up to 500 from the free preallocated range and only the new ranges are returned. The kernel skips the 6-byte header unchecked, ignores ranges below 0x1000 and fails the reply with -EIO above 8192 delegated inodes; libcephfs logs and discards them. Replies from the completed-request table for requests that created an inode carry the same extra. libcephfs verify_reply_trace re-resolves a traceless created inode with LOOKUP or GETATTR and returns -EINTR on an ino mismatch.
gates: client bit CEPHFS_FEATURE_DELEG_INO (13): Linux v5.7+, Ceph 15.2.0+
features.notes: Derived from code: with mds_allow_async_dirops turned off at runtime a raw 8-byte ino reaches clients that chose the openc_response_t parser, so every kernel CREATE reply fails with -EIO and libcephfs throws in DECODE_START (wire-protocol 8, kclient expectations 8). The member is read only in handle_conf_change, so a value set before startup is not applied until it changes at runtime. A retried MKNOD/MKDIR/SYMLINK found in the completed-request table outside clientreplay gets a traceless reply with this extra, which the kernel rejects with -EIO for those ops (narrow window, derived from code). Raw u64 users: kernels up to v5.6, Ceph up to 14.x. The kernel accepts a non-empty extra_bl only for GETFILELOCK, READDIR, LSSNAP, CREATE and GETVXATTR and fails the reply with -EIO otherwise. A CREATE that finds an existing name without O_EXCL is served as OPEN and carries no created ino, which is how both clients learn that the file already existed. See also F-CAPS-054 (delegation), F-NS-035 (CREATE), F-NS-012 (completed-request replies).

legacy_parts.note: Raw u64 created ino for sessions without bit 13; no created-ino extra for connections without REPLY_CREATE_INODE. Baseline clients advertise bit 13 and choose the openc_response_t parser from the MDS's bit 13, which is current with mds_allow_async_dirops true (default). The raw u64 created ino serves sessions without bit 13 (kernels up to v5.6, Ceph up to 14.x), and the empty extra serves connections without REPLY_CREATE_INODE (kernels before 3.9). With mds_allow_async_dirops false the raw u64 also reaches bit-13 clients, which then fail the reply.

features.name: GETFILELOCK, GETVXATTR and FILE_BLOCKDIFF extra payloads
features.summary: The remaining op-specific extra_bl formats; the kernel rejects a non-empty extra on any other op.
features.description: GETFILELOCK: raw 41-byte ceph_filelock {u64 start, length, client, owner, pid, u8 type} describing the conflicting lock, or type CEPH_LOCK_UNLOCK. GETVXATTR: ENCODE_START(1,1) {string value}, which the kernel requires to fill the section exactly. FILE_BLOCKDIFF: BlockDiff = ENCODE_START(1,1) {i32 rval, u64 scan_idx, interval_set<u64> blocks}. The kernel accepts extra_bl only for GETFILELOCK, READDIR, LSSNAP, CREATE and GETVXATTR (any other op with a non-empty extra is -EIO). Clients send GETVXATTR only to an MDS with bit 17 (otherwise -EOPNOTSUPP locally, mapped to -ENODATA by the kernel) and FILE_BLOCKDIFF only with bit 23.
gates: MDS bit CEPHFS_FEATURE_OP_GETVXATTR (17): Linux v6.1+ checks it, Ceph 16.2.11, 17.2.6, 18.2.0+
MDS bit CEPHFS_FEATURE_BLOCKDIFF (23): libcephfs only, Ceph 19.2.3, 20.2.0+
features.notes: Kernels v5.18-v6.0 send GETVXATTR without checking any bit ("The old ceph will crash the MDSs when see unknown OPs"). The ops themselves are owned by 04-namespace-and-posix-operations and 08-snapshots-quotas-subvolumes.

features.name: Early (unsafe) and safe replies
features.summary: A mutation is answered twice: an early unsafe reply as soon as it is applied in memory, and a safe reply once its journal event is committed.
features.description: Server::journal_and_reply calls early_reply before submitting the event. An early reply is sent unless mds_early_reply is false, the request set no_early_reply, it has journaled peers (multi-rank two-phase commit), its inode number came from the InoTable rather than the session's preallocated range, the requester is an MDS, or it is a replay; xlocks are marked done first so the uncommitted state becomes visible. The early reply carries the trace and extra_bl with safe = 0 and mdsmap_epoch = 0; the final reply after it carries only the result. Read-only and non-journaling ops get one safe reply with the trace; a re-executed REPLAY gets one traceless safe reply. The kernel applies the unsafe reply, keeps the request on the session unsafe list, does not parse the later safe reply and ignores duplicates; libcephfs links unsafe requests into session and inode lists and completes fsync waiters on the safe reply. Clients replay requests that got only an unsafe reply after an MDS failure; if the session is closed or the reconnect denied they are lost and the kernel marks the affected mappings -EIO.
features.notes: Perf counters measure latency to the first reply, i.e. to the early reply (wire-protocol 3.9.6). At most one unsafe and one safe reply per tid, unsafe before safe, on the session's current connection (wire-protocol 7). See also F-NS-011 (conditions), F-NS-010.

features.name: Reply content invariants enforced by clients
features.summary: Properties of trace content that clients check, some with a kernel BUG or an assert.
features.description: Kernel: a dentry trace whose directory differs from the request's locked parent in ino or snapid hits BUG_ON, a LOOKUPNAME dentry trace without target hits BUG_ON, inode numbers in [0x100, 0x1000) are refused with -EREMOTEIO, a changed inode type or device rdev gives -ESTALE, directories report nlink 1 and size 0 (the kernel shows 2 + subdirs). Version fields: version (2 x version + projected) is applied only if newer with an AUTH cap; size only decreases with a newer truncate_seq; mtime/atime only go back with a newer time_warp_seq; xattr_version and change_attr are monotonic; max_size is taken only from an auth cap; subvolume_id is immutable once non-zero. libcephfs applies the same version, cap and AUTH rules in add_update_inode and marks a directory complete when the reply shows it empty with Fs and without Fx.
features.notes: Kernel BUG paths reachable from MDS input are listed in kclient expectations 8. The C++ MDS uses nlink 1 for directories. Inode attribute semantics are owned by 05-metadata-cache-and-dirfrags.

features.name: MClientCaps encoding (v14, xattrs in the middle segment)
features.summary: Layout of the capability message exchanged in both directions; semantics belong to the capability model.
features.description: Front: raw 92-byte ceph_mds_caps_head {u32 op, u64 ino, realm, cap_id, u32 seq, issue_seq, caps, wanted, dirty, migrate_seq, u64 snap_follows, u32 snap_trace_len, uid, gid, mode, nlink, xattr_len, u64 xattr_version}, the 84-byte non-export body {size, max_size, truncate_size, truncate_seq, mtime, atime, ctime, legacy layout, time_warp_seq} or for EXPORT a 21-byte ceph_mds_cap_peer padded to 84 bytes, snap_trace_len bytes of snap trace, then v2 flockbl, v3 cap_peer (IMPORT), v4 inline_version + inline_data, v5 osd_epoch_barrier, v6 oldest_flush_tid, v7 caller_uid/gid, v8 pool_ns, v9 btime + change_attr, v10 flags (SYNC 1, PENDING_CAPSNAP 4), v11 nfiles/nsubdirs, v12 fscrypt_auth/file, v13 subvolume_id, v14 oserrno. The xattr blob is in the middle segment (xattr_len bytes). header.tid carries the client flush tid and is echoed in FLUSH_ACK/FLUSHSNAP_ACK. Ops: GRANT 0, REVOKE 1, TRUNC 2, EXPORT 3, IMPORT 4 (M to C); UPDATE 5, DROP 6, FLUSH 7, FLUSHSNAP 9, RELEASE 11, RENEW 12 (C to M); FLUSH_ACK 8, FLUSHSNAP_ACK 10 (M to C). The MDS encoder stops at v1 without FLOCK and v2 without EXPORT_PEER. Counted in push_seq.
features.notes: The kernel sends v12 (v6 up to v4.9, v10 in v4.10-v6.5) and parses up to v12, ignoring v13/v14; its snap trace starts right after a combined 176-byte head+body struct. Ceph clients send v8 (10.2.x), v10 (11.2-12.2.5), v11 (12.2.6-17.2.x), v12 (18.x-20.x), v13 (21.x tags), v14 (main); libcephfs sends only UPDATE and FLUSHSNAP. The decoder asserts middle length == xattr_len. Semantics owned by 03-caps-leases-and-locking. Message type CEPH_MSG_CLIENT_CAPS 0x310, HEAD_VERSION 14, COMPAT_VERSION 1. The EXPORT peer is ceph_mds_cap_peer {u64 cap_id, u32 issue_seq, u32 mseq, u32 mds, u8 flags}; flag NO_CAPSNAP (2) is unused. Without CEPH_FEATURE_MDS_INLINE_DATA (bit 40) the inline_data field is sent empty. _do_cap_update still applies a non-empty flockbl, but the kernel always sends a zero-length flock blob and in-tree libcephfs never sets it (other clients unverified). See also F-CAPS-011 (GRANT/REVOKE semantics), F-CAPS-013 (processing), F-STORE-098 (osd_epoch_barrier).

legacy_parts.note: Encoder stopping at v1 (no FLOCK) or v2 (no EXPORT_PEER); decoding client caps messages of versions other than 12 and 14; empty inline_data for connections without MDS_INLINE_DATA; non-empty inline_version/inline_data (deprecated inline_data setting). The MDS sends v14 to every baseline client and receives v12 from the 7.3 kernel and v14 from libcephfs at this commit. The v1/v2 encodings (no FLOCK or EXPORT_PEER) serve no client since Linux 2.6.36/3.14 and Ceph v0.75, other decoded versions (v6, v8, v10, v11, v13) come from older kernels and Ceph releases, and the empty inline_data without MDS_INLINE_DATA serves only kernels before 3.19. Non-empty inline data exists only after the deprecated inline_data file-system setting.

features.name: MClientCapRelease encoding and the OSD epoch barrier
features.summary: Batched cap releases from clients, carrying the client's OSD epoch barrier.
features.description: v2/compat 1: raw ceph_mds_cap_release {u32 num}, num x raw 24-byte ceph_mds_cap_item {u64 ino, u64 cap_id, u32 migrate_seq, u32 issue_seq}, then v2 u32 osd_epoch_barrier. Handled only in clientreplay, active or stopping (otherwise queued for replay); a non-zero barrier the Objecter does not have yet becomes an Objecter epoch barrier (RADOS ops paused until that OSDMap arrives) and raises the MDS barrier, which it then advertises in cap messages. The kernel batches up to 170 items per message; libcephfs sends them on each tick to ranks in clientreplay, active or stopping and on FLUSHMSG.
features.notes: Release semantics are owned by 03-caps-leases-and-locking; the OSD epoch barrier by 06-journal-and-storage. See also F-STORE-098 (OSD epoch barrier), F-CAPS-028 (batched cap release).

features.name: MClientLease encoding
features.summary: Layout of the dentry-lease control message and how each client uses its actions.
features.description: Raw 35-byte ceph_mds_lease {u8 action, u16 mask, u64 ino (parent dir), u64 first, u64 last, u32 seq, u32 duration_ms} + string dname. Actions: REVOKE 1 (M to C), RELEASE 2 (C to M), RENEW 3 (both), REVOKE_ACK 4 (C to M). The MDS revokes with mask 1 and last = CEPH_NOSNAP, answers RENEW with a fresh seq and duration if the lease is still grantable (counted), removes a lease on RELEASE/REVOKE_ACK only if seq matches, drops messages for unknown inodes, dentries or leases, and reaches ceph_abort() for any other action on a held lease. The kernel answers a revoke (and any lease message for an unknown inode or dentry) with REVOKE_ACK and sends RENEW; libcephfs asserts the action is REVOKE, answers RELEASE and never renews. Counted in push_seq.
features.notes: The revoke mask is "1 | CEPH_LOCK_DN" = 1 in userspace numbering; userspace and kernel CEPH_LOCK_* numbering differ, so no lock-type numbers can be exchanged with the kernel (wire-protocol 8). Lease semantics are owned by 03-caps-leases-and-locking. See also F-CAPS-042 (renew), F-CAPS-043 (revocation), F-CAPS-044 (expiry).

features.name: MClientSnap encoding
features.summary: Layout of snap realm update and split notifications, and what the MDS actually puts on the wire.
features.description: Raw 24-byte ceph_mds_snap_head {u32 op, u64 split, u32 num_split_inos, u32 num_split_realms, u32 trace_len}, then the split inos and split realms (u64 each) and trace_len bytes of snap trace. Ops UPDATE 0, CREATE 1, DESTROY 2, SPLIT 3. Per-realm notifications (mksnap, rmsnap, renamesnap, realm creation, realm moves by link/unlink/rename) always use op SPLIT with split = the realm inode and that client's trace, with split lists filled only for a real split; realm split/merge also send SPLIT; a committed snap-table transaction sends every open or stale session UPDATE (DESTROY for rmsnap) for the global snaprealm inode 3; UPDATE is also the reconnect catch-up. CREATE is never sent. All sends are counted. libcephfs asserts that nothing follows the trace and that a SPLIT trace starts with head.split.
features.notes: Snapshot semantics are owned by 08-snapshots-quotas-subvolumes. See also F-SNAP-009 (per-realm notifications) and F-SNAP-010 (global realm broadcast).

features.name: MClientQuota encoding
features.summary: Layout of the quota and recursive-statistics push to clients holding caps on a quota realm inode.
features.description: Payload: u64 ino, utime rctime, i64 rbytes, i64 rfiles, i64 rsubdirs, quota_info_t ENCODE_START(1,1) {i64 max_bytes, i64 max_files}; rsnaps is not sent. MDCache::broadcast_quota_to_client sends it from the auth rank (active or stopping, inode not frozen, quota enabled or just changed) to cap holders not marked noquota: unconditionally on quota updates, otherwise when rstat changed and usage reached (bytes: within 1/8 of) the limit or moved by more than 1/16 of the remaining distance since the last notification. Counted in push_seq. libcephfs replaces quota and rstat wholesale (zeroing rsnaps until the next InodeStat); both clients enforce quotas locally.
features.notes: MClientQuota asserts on trailing bytes in the C++ decoder. Quota semantics are owned by 08-snapshots-quotas-subvolumes. See also F-SNAP-045 (push policy and thresholds).

legacy_parts.note: Skipping cap holders marked noquota (Capability STATE_NOQUOTA, set for connections without MDS_QUOTA). Both baseline client families negotiate MDS_QUOTA (bit 47), so no baseline cap is marked noquota and every quota-realm cap holder receives MClientQuota. The noquota exclusion applies only to connections without MDS_QUOTA (kernels before 4.17).

features.name: MClientMetrics encoding and client send rules
features.summary: Layout of the client metrics upload and when each client sends it.
features.description: Payload: u32 count of ClientMetricMessage, each u32 metric_type + a payload wrapped in ENCODE_START; types 0 CAP_INFO, 1 READ_LATENCY, 2 WRITE_LATENCY, 3 METADATA_LATENCY, 4 DENTRY_LEASE, 5 OPENED_FILES, 6 PINNED_ICAPS, 7 OPENED_INODES, 8 READ_IO_SIZES, 9 WRITE_IO_SIZES, 10-15 average/stdev types (no MDS decoder), 16 SUBVOLUME_METRICS (ENCODE_START(1,1) {u64 count, count x AggregatedIOMetrics {subvolume_id, read/write counts, bytes, latency_us, time_stamp}}); unknown types are skipped by their length. The MDS processes it in MetricsHandler without mds_lock and drops it while the rank is not active. The kernel sends once per second to one session with METRIC_COLLECT whose rank is exactly up:active (with subvolume metrics, also bit 22), and its type 16 item is a bare u32 type followed by the payload; libcephfs sends every tick to rank 0 only (priority CEPH_MSG_PRIO_HIGH - 1), including only the types in the MDS metric spec.
gates: MDS bit CEPHFS_FEATURE_METRIC_COLLECT (14): Linux v5.9+, Ceph 16.2.0+
MDS metric spec bit 16 (libcephfs subvolume metrics)
features.notes: Without METRIC_COLLECT the kernel never sends metrics ("MDS will close the session's socket"). libcephfs subtracts a CLOCK_REALTIME stamp from a CLOCK_MONOTONIC one for metadata latency, so that metric is not a real latency (libcephfs-fuse-ganesha 8). Metrics aggregation is owned by 10-qos-metrics-quiesce-quarantine. The kernel ignores failed ops except -ENOENT and -ETIMEDOUT in its latency statistics. Each rank that holds a session but receives no metrics for it forwards zeroed values to rank 0 (F-QOS-014). See also F-QOS-011 (negotiation), F-QOS-012 (ingestion).

features.name: MQuarantineDisable encoding
features.summary: Layout of the notification that lifts quarantine on an inode for clients that understand quarantine.
features.description: Payload: u64 ino, i32 oserrno (always 0, tells the client to clear its per-inode error). Sent counted, only to sessions with CEPHFS_FEATURE_QUARANTINE (24), when quarantine is lifted on an inode they hold caps on. libcephfs handles it in Client::handle_quarantine_disable without counting it and without checking which session it came from.
gates: client bit CEPHFS_FEATURE_QUARANTINE (24): no kernel, no Ceph release tag yet (main only)
features.notes: The counting mismatch makes a later libcephfs REQUEST_CLOSE carry a seq below push_seq, which the MDS drops (derived from code; F-PROTO-050). Quarantine is owned by 10-qos-metrics-quiesce-quarantine. Message type CEPH_MSG_CLIENT_QUARANTINE_DISABLE (0x315), head and compat version 1; the kernel never receives it (it would only log an unknown type). After the dropped REQUEST_CLOSE the C++ client gives up after client_shutdown_timeout (30 s) and the session lingers until it goes stale (code reading, not covered by tests). See also F-QOS-077 (when quarantine sends it).

features.group: Client-specific expectations (kclient, libcephfs, ceph-fuse, NFS-Ganesha, Samba)
features.name: Mount flow requirements
features.summary: What a mount sends to the MDS before any application request: map subscription, root GETATTR by a root-relative path, and ancestor lookups.
features.description: The kernel subscribes to the mdsmap (or fsmap.user and mdsmap.<fscid> with mds_namespace; a name mismatch shuts the mount down), keeps requests waiting while the map epoch is 0, fails them with -EHOSTUNREACH when no rank is active unless norequire_active_mds is set, and opens the root with GETATTR on path (1, server path without leading "/"), mask PIN, any rank, timeout mount_timeout (60 s); the target inode becomes the superblock root, so mounting depends on GETATTR resolving a root-relative multi-component path. libcephfs fails the mount with -EACCES if the MDSMap has refuse_client_session, then issues GETATTR (CEPH_STAT_CAP_INODE_ALL) on the mount path and on each ancestor up to "/" so quota realms above the mount are visible (-EACCES on an ancestor is tolerated). ceph-fuse first waits for the cluster to be available (fuse_require_active_mds). Sessions are opened lazily by the first request.
gates: kernel mount options mds_namespace, require_active_mds, mount_timeout
features.notes: Mount-time GETATTRs from libcephfs run with caller_uid/gid -1 unless client_mount_uid/gid are set (libcephfs-fuse-ganesha 8).

features.group: Client-specific expectations (kclient, libcephfs, ceph-fuse, NFS-Ganesha, Samba)
features.name: Inode-number addressed access (NFS file handles, #ino paths, LOOKUPINO)
features.summary: NFS servers and libcephfs address objects by inode number; the MDS resolves any inode number a client presents.
features.description: libcephfs builds almost every request relative to an inode number (#ino or #parent/name). Ganesha file handles carry {ino, snapid, fscid}; on a cache miss ceph_ll_lookup_vino sends LOOKUPINO to rank rand() % num_in with the mount's default credentials (uid/gid -1 unless set), with args.lookupino.snapid for snapped inodes, and LOOKUPPARENT resolves ".." of a handle-only directory. The kernel NFS export uses LOOKUPINO (fh_to_dentry, with snapid, parent and hash for snapped handles; a reply whose snapid differs is treated as unsupported), LOOKUPPARENT (get_parent) and LOOKUPNAME (get_name; reply needs dentry and target). The MDS opens uncached inodes for LOOKUPINO with open_ino and returns -ESTALE for purging or MDS-private inodes. Inodes known only by handle have no path to the mount root, so libcephfs cannot evaluate MDS auth caps locally: their setattr is never buffered and every open goes to the MDS.
features.notes: Ganesha never causes LOOKUPHASH or LOOKUPNAME (libcephfs-fuse-ganesha 3.16.5). LOOKUPINO semantics are owned by 04-namespace-and-posix-operations.

features.group: Client-specific expectations (kclient, libcephfs, ceph-fuse, NFS-Ganesha, Samba)
features.name: Inode number ranges clients accept
features.summary: Constraints on the inode numbers an MDS hands out, imposed by the kernel reserved range and by ceph-fuse inode numbering.
features.description: The kernel refuses inode numbers in [0x100, 0x1000) (MDS-reserved: mdsdirs, logs, strays) with -EREMOTEIO in replies and -ESTALE in NFS paths, and ignores delegated ranges starting below 0x1000; libcephfs returns -ESTALE locally for reserved vinos. ceph-fuse exposes FUSE inode numbers (stag << 48) | ino, with stag 0 for head, 1 for snapdir and other values mapped per snapid, so MDS inode numbers at or above 2^48 alias in FUSE (unless client_use_faked_inos) and one inode can be exposed under at most 65534 snapids at a time (else ceph_abort_msg("run out of stag")).
features.notes: See also F-STORE-046 (special inode numbers).

features.group: Client-specific expectations (kclient, libcephfs, ceph-fuse, NFS-Ganesha, Samba)
features.name: Shared sessions: NFS-Ganesha and Samba libcephfsd
features.summary: One MDS session per rank can carry the requests of many NFS clients or SMB processes, distinguished only by credentials in each request.
features.description: FSAL_CEPH (nfs-ganesha V15.7) creates one cmount per {filesystem, cmount_path, user_id, key} and shares it among exports; mgr/nfs gives all exports of one (cluster, fs, cmount_path) the same cephx user and defaults cmount_path to "/", so by default a Ganesha daemon holds one session per rank per file system. Many NFS worker threads have requests outstanding on that session at once, distinguished by caller_uid/gid and gid_list; requests can reach a rank out of tid order. ceph_ll_open always runs as uid 0/gid 0 (ceph_reopen_func), so every OPEN Ganesha issues through it, and the lock and read/write-path requests on such an Fh, are checked as root (a root_squash MDS cap grant refuses Ganesha write opens unless another grant matches); lock owners are Ganesha object addresses with pid 0 and Ganesha never sends a blocking lock. Samba vfs_ceph_new with proxy=yes goes through the in-tree libcephfsd daemon, which shares one libcephfs mount among SMB processes with identical configuration.
features.notes: Derived from code (libcephfs-fuse-ganesha 8): Ganesha opens as uid 0, and a write through such an Fh never clears setuid/setgid bits through libcephfs. FSAL_CEPH sets client_acl_type=posix_acl and client_oc (default false) on every cmount. The SMB server source is not in the repository.

features.group: Client-specific expectations (kclient, libcephfs, ceph-fuse, NFS-Ganesha, Samba)
features.name: NFS-Ganesha delegations built on caps
features.summary: NFSv4 delegations in Ganesha are implemented inside libcephfs by holding cap references; the MDS sees only cap revokes that take longer to be acknowledged.
features.description: ceph_set_deleg_timeout(t) (t < session_autoclose, else -EINVAL) enables delegations per mount; Inode::set_deleg grants a read delegation only with PIN, As, Ls, Xs, Fs, Fr, Fc already issued (write adds Fx, Fw, Fb) and holds cap references, so those caps are not released. A revoke of a delegated cap (or a conflicting local open, unlink, link or rename) invokes the application recall callback; the revoke is acknowledged only after the delegation is returned, and after deleg_timeout without return the whole client is force-unmounted. With delegations enabled a successful OPEN also waits until Fr/Fw are actually issued. FSAL_CEPH V15.7 enables them only with NFSv4 Delegations = true (timeout Lease_Lifetime * 2 + 5, 125 s by default) and returns a recalled delegation from a fridge thread right after the callback; the cephadm template disables delegations. The MDS has no delegation-specific code.
gates: Ganesha NFSv4 Delegations (default false; cephadm template false)
features.notes: mds_cap_revoke_eviction_timeout (default 0) would evict a client holding a revoke longer than that. The client_deleg_timeout option named in the libcephfs documentation is not defined (libcephfs-fuse-ganesha 5.2). Cap revocation is owned by 03-caps-leases-and-locking. Delegations depend on ordinary GRANT/REVOKE and the loner/EXCL policy (F-CAPS-005, F-CAPS-011).

features.group: Cluster client libraries sharing the MDS identity (MonClient, MgrClient, Objecter)
features.name: MonClient obligations
features.summary: How the MDS process talks to the monitors as a client: bootstrap, hunting, authentication, tickets, subscriptions, commands and the cluster log.
features.description: Before the daemon exists, global_init fetches the MonMap and MConfig on a temporary CLIENT-typed messenger with the MDS key.
