The MonClient then hunts mon_client_hunt_parallel (3) monitors every mon_client_hunt_interval (3 s, backoff x1.5 up to x10) and keeps the first that authenticates; it sends keepalives every 10 s and re-hunts after 30 s without KEEPALIVE2_ACK or on reset. It authenticates with msgr2 AUTH_MODE_MON (10) + EntityName + global_id (msgr1: MAuth with CEPH_AUTH_UNKNOWN), presenting the previous auth ticket so the global id (the FSMap gid) is kept, requests tickets for MON, OSD, MDS and MGR and renews them at three quarters of their validity. Subscriptions: monmap, config, mdsmap (from 0), mgrmap (from the first FSMap appearance), osdmap (Objecter); the monitor serves the mdsmap subscription by exact address-vector match against the FSMap. MConfig is applied, MLog entries carry sequence numbers and are dropped only on MLogAck, pending MMonCommands are resent on a new session, queued messages are dropped on re-hunt, and MMonGetVersion serves map waits. MDS code calls the MonClient while holding mds_lock (order mds_lock then monc_lock).
features.notes: A new global id means a new gid, which the FSMap treats as a different daemon (transport page 8, item 21). MonClient subscriptions and beacons are owned by 01-cluster-membership-and-ha; the transport page lists the full duty table (3.7). See also F-CLU-110 (MonClient subscriptions).

legacy_parts.note: msgr1 monitor authentication (MonConnection::start sending MAuth with CEPH_AUTH_UNKNOWN). The MDS binds msgr2 and authenticates to monitors at this commit over msgr2 with AUTH_MODE_MON. The MAuth exchange with protocol CEPH_AUTH_UNKNOWN is used only on a msgr1 connection to a monitor.

features.group: Cluster client libraries sharing the MDS identity (MonClient, MgrClient, Objecter)
features.name: MgrClient obligations
features.summary: How the MDS process reports to the active manager: session open keyed by daemon name, configure, and periodic perf-counter reports.
features.description: When the daemon first appears in the FSMap the MgrClient starts and subscribes to mgrmap; on each new active mgr it connects (lossy, secure mode by default, at most once per mgr_connect_retry_interval, 1 s) and sends MMgrOpen v3 (daemon_name = <id>, empty service name, running config and defaults). The mgr keys the session as ("mds", id) and disconnects until it has fetched mds metadata from the monitor. MMgrConfigure (stats_period from mgr_stats_period 5 s, stats_threshold 5, OSD and MDS perf-metric queries) starts the report timer; every period an MMgrReport v9 declares new counters (path, description, nick, type, priority, unit) and packs values in lexicographic order of the declared paths, with undeclare lists, config when changed, task_status (scrub status, every 2 s while non-empty) and the rank 0 metric report. The mgr requires SERVER_LUMINOUS from MDS peers and ignores daemon_health_metrics from an MDS; mgr modules never open connections to an MDS (they use libcephfs).
features.notes: MMgrReport.packed has no per-value keys, so a different packing order shifts every value on the mgr side (transport page 8, item 26). Perf counters and mgr modules are owned by 11-security-admin-and-observability, the metric report by 10-qos-metrics-quiesce-quarantine. See also F-ADM-067 (counter reporting).

features.group: Cluster client libraries sharing the MDS identity (MonClient, MgrClient, Objecter)
features.name: Objecter obligations (OSD client protocol)
features.summary: How the MDS process reads and writes RADOS: OSDMap following, placement, resend and pause rules, epoch barrier, backoffs and fencing.
features.description: The Objecter applies OSDMap incrementals in epoch order (full maps when an incremental is missing, skipping trimmed epochs and then resending every op), re-targets every op on each epoch with placement identical to the C++ OSDMap/CRUSH code (object hash, stable_mod, crush rule, upmaps, primary affinity, pg_temp), resends on interval change, split/merge, forced resend or unpause, pauses reads on PAUSERD, writes on PAUSEWR and everything while the map epoch is below its epoch barrier (set_epoch_barrier only raises it). The MDS ignores pool full flags (FULL_FORCE on every op). MOSDOp is encoded by the OSD connection features (v9 with SERVER_SQUID, v8, v7); replies with a stale retry_attempt are ignored, redirects resubmitted, -EAGAIN resent to the primary. With RADOS_BACKOFF, BLOCK is acknowledged with ACK_BLOCK, ops in the blocked range are held and resent on UNBLOCK. OSD sessions are lossy: a reset reopens the session and resends all ops in tid order; laggy ops (older than objecter_timeout, 10 s) trigger an MPing. -EBLOCKLISTED (108) means the MDS has been fenced and it respawns.
features.notes: The MDS-specific RADOS operation catalogue and full handling are owned by 06-journal-and-storage. librados is a separate identity (client.<global_id>, own nonce, client_inc 0), unlike the Objecter embedded in the MDS messenger (transport page 8, item 30). See also F-STORE-090 (per-rank Objecter).

legacy_parts.note: MOSDOp encodings v8 and older, chosen from OSD connection features. OSDs at this commit advertise SERVER_SQUID (in CEPH_FEATURES_ALL), so the Objecter encodes MOSDOp as v9. The v8 encoding (no SERVER_SQUID, OSDs older than 19.x), v7 (no RESEND_ON_SPLIT) and older encodings serve only OSDs of older releases in a mixed-version cluster.

features.group: Cluster client libraries sharing the MDS identity (MonClient, MgrClient, Objecter)
features.name: Fencing identity: one address vector for clients, monitors and OSDs
features.summary: Monitors find the MDS and OSDs fence it by address, so the address vector the MDS beacons is the one it presents on every connection.
features.description: The monitor serves an MDS-named session's mdsmap subscription by searching the FSMap for the daemon whose mds_info_t::addrs equal the session's address vector (msgr2 CLIENT_IDENT addrvec or msgr1 banner address); a daemon not found gets an empty map or only its standby entry. On failover the monitor blocklists every address in the failed daemon's addrs (only for a daemon that held a rank and was not in standby-replay), and an OSD rejects ops with -EBLOCKLISTED when the connection's first peer address matches the blocklist exactly, by IP, or by range. The C++ MDS satisfies both with its single messenger: msgr2 CLIENT_IDENT carries messenger->get_myaddrs() and the msgr1 banner get_myaddr_legacy(); MDS OSD traffic also carries the entity mds.<rank> and client_inc = the MDSMap incarnation.
features.notes: An MDS whose mon-session address vector differs from its beaconed addrs receives no MDSMap for its file system (transport page 8, item 24). Failover fencing is owned by 01-cluster-membership-and-ha. See also F-CLU-036 (blocklist fencing).

legacy_parts.note: Identity presented in the msgr1 banner (legacy address) on msgr1 connections to monitors and OSDs. The MDS's MonClient and Objecter connect over msgr2, where CLIENT_IDENT carries the full address vector that the monitor matches against the FSMap and OSDs fence. The msgr1 banner address (get_myaddr_legacy) is the presented identity only on msgr1 connections.

features.summary: Transport settings between MDS daemons of the same file system; the project constraint means only the new daemons speak this protocol to each other.
features.description: C++ uses Policy::lossless_peer(CEPH_FEATURE_UID) for MDS peers (no resetcheck), protocol 36 (CEPH_MDS_PROTOCOL) on msgr1, the cluster auth method and ms_cluster_mode (crc by default), and connection-race resolution by address order (WAIT) in both protocols. MDSRank::send_message_mds first sends its MDSMap to a peer whose known epoch is older; peers whose address left the map or whose incarnation changed are marked down. MDS-to-MDS messages flow only between daemons of the same file system.
features.notes: The new MDS never runs mixed with C++ MDS daemons in one file system, so no C++ daemon expects this protocol from it (transport page 7.8). Inter-rank messages are owned by 07-multi-mds. See also F-CLU-109, F-CLU-072.

legacy_parts.note: msgr1 protocol number 36 (CEPH_MDS_PROTOCOL) check and msgr1 connection-race resolution by legacy address. C++ MDS daemons at this commit connect to the v2 address each peer publishes first, and msgr2 has no protocol-number check. The protocol number 36 check (BADPROTOVER) and the msgr1 race rule by legacy address order apply only to msgr1 connections between MDS daemons.
